### Resume 127 (OPUS) - the widget sweep adds no new instance, and that is its result

`OPUS-WIDGET-SWEEP-AND-COMMIT-MISMATCH` (P1) asked to turn the hand-found embedded-widget
signature into a sweep. Done, over all 65 census artifacts, and the honest headline is that it
**confirms six known instances mechanically and finds none that survives scrutiny**.

**The signature, mechanised.** A base B is a widget base when accesses at B+d, d inside the
`0xC0` header, *begin* on declared Widget field starts and none begins mid-field — with a wider
access sound when it *ends* on a declared boundary, because the compiler merges adjacent fields.
Candidate bases are **derived** as `access_offset - row_offset`, not scanned, which is exact and
is what makes 65 artifacts affordable.

**Three controls.** NEGATIVE: every artifact is also scored against decoy layouts carrying the
same multiset of row sizes and gaps, shuffled — real **47** clean bases, decoys **0.25 per
layout**. POSITIVE: Widget's own census scores **35 of 35** declared rows at `+0x0` over 347
accesses, and a decoy on the same data scores 4 exact against 165 interior violations.
CONTAINMENT: `base + 0xC0` must fit the declared type size, which alone refutes
`ItemClassDescriptor +0x8` — a `0xC0` header cannot sit at `+0x8` of a `0x58`-byte type.

### Resume 128 (OPUS) - a widget's extent is an argument, and _8FA0's size stops being a ceiling

The sized-by-argument ctype rule needs a row's own width to CARRY an instance extent, and every
embedded instance in this store had a **floor**. Floors do not satisfy that rule. But a widget's
size is not something to infer at all - **it is passed to the in-place constructor in `edx`**.

`00245000` takes `rcx` = caller-owned storage, `edx` = size, `r8` = handler, and a fifth
argument always 1, which sets bit 14 of `+0x40` meaning *storage the widget does not own* -
i.e. embedded. So the extent of an embedded instance is readable at its construction site.

**`scan_widget_inplace_extents.py`** (kit, `--self-test`) recovers the `lea rcx, [base+disp]`
and the `mov edx, imm` at every construction site: 40 in-place, 9 sized, 231 factory. Fifteen
in-place sites give an offset **and** a literal extent outright.

#### What it confirms, and what was already there (OPUS)

It cross-validates against four independently established facts: `003F9FA4`/`003F9FEC` give
`rbx+0xD0` and `rbx+0x1A0`, both extent `0xD0` — `_57E0`'s two in-place widgets, previously
derived from *spacing* and now read from the argument; `002766E0` asks `0x61F0`, exactly
`_AB30`'s declared size; `0027A42D` asks `0x3010`, exactly its documented child stride; and two
sites ask `0xBC08`, matching the store's record.

**And the size table already existed.** `Tools/work/h78/widget_constructor_sites.tsv` has
carried 49 sites and 26 sizes all along. My scan reproduces it exactly — **40 common sites,
zero size disagreements**. What that table does *not* carry is the `lea rcx`, so no site had
ever been bound to a storage offset. **The binding is the contribution; the numbers are not
new.** Third time today I have re-derived something the store already held.

#### The result: `_8FA0` 0x1130 → 0x1110 (OPUS)

Read end to end: `00291750` does `lea rcx, [rdi+0x8fa0]` at `002917AA` and calls `002BE450`;
`002BE450` is six instructions, **never writes `rcx`** — so it forwards its caller's storage,
the wrapper shape this store already documents at the factory — and does `mov edx, 0x1110`
before `call 00245000`. It has **exactly one caller**. So a `0x1110`-byte widget is constructed
in place at singleton+`0x8FA0`, which is this object.

The row had asked for this itself: *"THE SIZE IS A CEILING… the next sibling starts 0x1130 on"*.
A distance to the next sibling is an upper bound, not an extent. `0x1110` is also one of the 26
enumerated widget sizes.

**Consequence, exact and small:** `0x8FA0 + 0x1110 = 0xA0B0`, the next sibling starts at
`0xA0D0`, so **0x20 bytes belong to neither**. `unobservedTail1100` shrinks 48 → 16, and the
parent's `embedded8FA0` row shrinks 4400 → 4368 with the remainder declared as `paddingA0B0`
rather than absorbed. Leaving it inside the parent's row would have kept the layout tiling and
hidden the difference — a gap is a question, not a label.

**What this does not do:** it does not declare the widget *instances* inside `_8FA0`. `+0xAC0`
still has a floor of `0x584` and no binding, because **no in-place site in the image carries
`lea rcx, [reg + 0xAC0]`**. The outer object's extent is closed; the inner instances are not.

### Resume 129 (OPUS) - a second extent bound, and the six ceilings that will not bind

Two small results, one positive and one negative, both from pushing the extent-binding method
past the single case that motivated it.

**The arg0-alias step, and why the first resolver missed half the shape.** A body that never
writes `rcx` forwards its own first argument — that is how `_8FA0`'s `0x1110` was bound through
`002BE450`. But a body that **saves `rcx` into a register and restores it later** is forwarding
just as much, and the first version of the resolver treated it as unresolvable. Tracking which
registers still alias the entry `rcx` took the bound count from 1 to 2.

**`_AB30`'s `0x61F0` is a measured extent, not a ceiling.** `00276650` reaches `002766E0` with
`mov edx, 0x61F0` then `call 00245000`; its `rcx` is its own saved-and-restored first argument,
and its **single** caller passes `rbx + 0xAB30`. So a `0x61F0`-byte widget is constructed in
place at singleton+`0xAB30`, and the declared size and the asked-for size agree exactly.

That agreement is the point. **Eight of these sibling types declare a size that is only the
distance to the next sibling**, and each says so in its own evidence: *"THE SIZE IS A CEILING…
the next sibling starts X on"*. `_AB30` is not one of them, and now that is proven rather than
assumed.

#### The bounded negative, recorded so nobody repeats it (OPUS)

The six siblings still carrying a ceiling — `_00A0`, `_5380`, `_57E0`, `_7EA0`, `_7FB0`,
`_A0D0` — **do not bind by either available route**, and I tried both:

1. No in-place widget construction site in the image carries a `lea rcx` at any of their
   offsets, so the `00245000` `edx` argument that bound `_8FA0` and `_AB30` is unavailable.
2. A scan of **every** function body for the store's other binding — a clear of a literal size
   at a sibling offset, `lea rcx,[base+off]` then `call 00275550`, the shape
   `_57E0ArrayRecord`'s route was verified with — returns **zero** for all six.

So those six keep a floor and a ceiling, which is better than narrowing one of them by
argument. Recorded on each row rather than left as an absence.

and a nonzero 32-bit value is a **valid low address**. ASTRA is right.

### Resume 134 (OPUS) - the producer test, finally run, and its sharp case is a negative

I named this test three times before running it: is an encoded arena reference **runtime-produced**
by something calling the encoder `0020E620`, or **authored**, arriving from file data? The codec
cannot tell them apart - only the producer can.

**The general result is the useful half.** Of **767** encoder call sites, **699 store the result
straight into a structure field** and 68 do not. Encoding a pointer and writing it into a field
is overwhelmingly what this engine does with the encoder, so an encoded reference field is *as a
rule* runtime-produced rather than authored.

**The sharp case is a negative, and I stated the limits before running it.** `+0x94` does receive
an encoder result at five sites - `0037142A`/`00371462` in `003713C0`, `0037290F`/`0037299A` in
`00372820`, `004317B8` in `00431770` - and **none of them is `RenderStrideC0Element`**. Those
three functions are cited by no row of it and appear in **no census artifact anywhere in the
store**. A displacement is not a type, and `+0x94` is a common offset.

So the row's own long-standing statement survives intact - *"the constructor does not touch it,
and the census found no writer anywhere"* - and what is added is that **the encoder-then-store
pattern is excluded** as that writer. A producer test that finds no producer does not make a
field authored; it removes one candidate mechanism.

*Method limits, recorded with the result rather than after it:* following stops at the first
overwrite of EAX and at any call, ret or jmp, so a producer that parks the value in another
register first, or stores it later, is invisible to this pass.

### The instrument finding, which outlived the request (OPUS)

`ImageAddressArenaRecord` is routed `ARRAY 0x022D7FD0 stride=0xA8 count=15` and its committed
census artifact held **one row**. I assumed a blind spot and went looking for it, and it was not
where I expected: `gen_route_seeded_census.py` **already models** an ARRAY route's computed
element base. `Census.stride` has done so since it was written, and its own comment says that
shape "is why seventeen ARRAY-routed types had no census". **Nothing ever set it** - `parse_route`
accepted PTR/FN/STATIC only, so every ARRAY route fell out at "not one this tool models". The
store holds **19 ARRAY routes over 17 distinct types**: the comment's own number, still exact.
The capability was written, documented, defaulted off, and never wired up.

Wiring the parser to the machinery: **1 row -> 41 accesses at 26 offsets in 5 functions**, and
**13 of those offsets fell inside spans declared "no censused access"**.

**And the one row it did hold was not an access to the type.** It was `0036C5C1`,
`mov qword ptr [rax + 0xa0], rdx` - reached through `xor eax,eax` on `0036C5A0`'s out-of-bounds
path, base **zero**, a deliberate null-write trap for an id above 14. `tailQword00A0` cited that
trap as its evidence. The genuine element write is `0036C5B6`, where the element base is folded
into the memory operand (`[rcx + rax + 0xa0]`) and materialised in no register at all - a third
form of computed base, now modelled too, strictly at scale 1 so an inner array's subscript stays
refused.

*Two controls, both fixed before the run:* a PTR census regenerated afterwards is **byte-identical**
(no existing artifact moved), and `+0x02` and `+0x68` - the two offsets I had read out of
`00369860` by hand - both appear. Fourteen of the nineteen referencing functions still contribute
nothing, and I checked rather than assumed why: `0036B060` is a pure `arenaRecordById(id)`
accessor that dereferences nothing. The residue is accessors, not missed fields.

**The other sixteen ARRAY-routed types are NOT re-censused.** Reachable is not done.

### Resume 137 (OPUS) - why seven types censused zero, and the instrument gap behind two of them

Chasing the sweep's seven zeros found **two different causes**, and the difference matters
because only one of them is the instrument's fault.

`ScriptNativeDispatchRecord`'s base `0x01EED708` has **zero references image-wide** against a
passing control. Nothing names it, so no walk can start; that is a question about the route, not
about the tool.

`ChunkedSlotEntry` and `ChunkedSlotBankEntry` are a tool gap, and a precise one. `00477EE0`
passes both to `0051F9F0` as the **6th and 5th arguments - on the stack** (`mov [rsp+0x28], rax`
/ `mov [rsp+0x20], rax`), and the walk propagates a tracked pointer into a callee only through
`ARG_REGS`. So both are dropped at the call and their accesses, which all happen inside the
callee, are invisible.

**The slot-to-type mapping was checked, not assumed, and the check caught my own slip.** I first
read `[rsp+0x50]` at `0051FA0A` as the 6th argument. Resolving the prologue (`push r14` +
`sub rsp,0x20` = 0x28) makes it `entry_rsp+0x28`, the **5th** - `02CA74A0`,
`ChunkedSlotBankEntry` - and the loop that walks it steps `lea rax,[rax+0x20]`, which **matches
that type's declared stride of 0x20**. The stride is what confirmed the arithmetic. The 6th is
read at `0051FA7C` and stored to the object `+0x38`.

So both tables are **installed into a runtime object** (`+0x10` and `+0x38`) and every later
access goes through it - their `ARRAY` route says where the table IS, not how it is REACHED.

**And the obvious fix is wrong.** Seeding `0051F9F0` directly would work mechanically, but it
has three callers - `00409F10`, `0046E250`, `00477EE0`, all render-root sub-initialisers, each
supplying its own table pair - so a census seeded there conflates three instances. That is the
conflation `emit_seeded_census.py`'s own docstring already records as measured, 43 offsets
against 26. Filed as `OPUS-PROPOSE-CENSUS-STACK-ARGUMENT-SEEDING` rather than built half-way,
and the limit is now stated in the tool's docstring so a zero is not read as absence.

### The real finding is an extent (OPUS)

`embeddedDestroyedSubObject3E0` was declared **64** bytes. Its own functions reach `+0x98`:

`006336E0` reads and clears `[rbx+0x78]` and `[rbx+0x98]`. Both top out at `+0x98` with an 8-byte

**This is reattribution, not gap-consumption.** Those 96 bytes were never this type's own fields;

nested base is "a field of a NESTED object, not a field of this one". The child's internals stay

### Resume 140 (OPUS) - is anything else polymorphic? One thing, and I re-derived the answer

The vtable census worked so well on `CharacterRenderObject` that the obvious move was to
generalise it. It does not generalise: **the store names a vtable for exactly one non-Phyre
type**, the one just done. So I went looking for the vtables instead - every non-Phyre type
whose `ctor` column is an address, constructor disassembled, checked for the MSVC install
pattern `lea rX,[rip->T]` then a store to `[this]`. Control: `CharacterRenderObject`'s ctor must
yield `00903B68`, which the store records independently. It does.

    constructor installs a vtable            1
    constructor read, no vtable install     63
    rejected by the shape test               2
    ctor column DECLARES there is none      22   <- a resolved negative
    ctor column names no usable address     20   <- never looked
                                           ---
    non-Phyre types with a ctor column     108   exhaustive, nothing dropped

**A shape test was needed and the first run was wrong without it.** Matching `lea` + store-at-
offset-0 alone reported `ImageAddressArenaRecord`'s vtable as `022D7FD0` - the **arena record
table in `.data`** - and `Category`'s as `01CB4490`, which turned out to be a
`[sead][!error!!]` **diagnostic descriptor**, `{fn, info, fn, 0}` followed by the message text
naming `Category::InitializeRef`. A vtable is not merely an address stored at offset 0.
Requiring `.rdata` **and** three `.text` slots rejects both, and the tool now prints the
rejections with their reasons rather than dropping them.

**THE CONCLUSION IS ALREADY IN THE DATABASE.** `rtti-vtable-object-model.md` §6 established on
2026-09-02, under falsification, that *"the engine is C++ with reflection; the game on top of it
is C with tables"* - gameplay owners at zero virtual methods. I reached the same place by a
different count. **Tenth re-derivation this session**, and the first one I stopped *before*
publishing as new: I checked the document because the `Category` trail led to
`sead-engine-identity-and-diagnostics.md`, which also turned out to hold everything I had just
worked out about `Category` - its RTTI name `SQEX::Sd::ConfigFile::Category` and
`Category::InitializeRefCategory` at `007AA320`. Its `ctor` column even records the two
addresses the constructor installs.

**What IS new is about the store, not the image.** **20** types have a `ctor` column that is
prose - *"the resource loader"*, *"its owning array's initialisation"* - so for those *"no
vtable"* was never tested, which is a different claim from *"not polymorphic"*. The gap is in
the column.

**I first counted 36, and that was my tool's error, caught before it published.** A bare hex
search matched addresses sitting inside *prose explaining why there is no constructor*.
`ActorManagerSlot` came out as naming `02098E10`, its table base - but its column reads *"none

this cell held 02098E10, which is the storage address, not a constructor"*. **The column was
right and already carried its own correction, and my tool matched the correction's
explanation.** A column that says "none" is an answer; it now has its own bucket, and eight
types moved out of the address bucket with it. The eleventh time this session that the store
already knew - this one caught by reading the row before acting on the tool.

Recorded as COVERAGE-DIMENSIONS 6b, with the corroboration explicitly framed as agreeing with
the 2026-09-02 finding rather than extending it. The sweep is promoted to the kit as
`find_type_vtables.py` with its control, so the next person runs it instead of rebuilding it -

### Resume 141 (OPUS) - the stack-argument seed, built and falsified-first

My own proposal, so I decided it by building it. The walk propagated a tracked pointer into a
callee only through `ARG_REGS`, so a table handed over as argument five or six - on the stack -
was invisible, and `ChunkedSlotEntry` and `ChunkedSlotBankEntry` censused **zero**.

**The risk I wrote into the proposal is the part I handled first.** The fifth argument lives at
`entry_rsp + 0x28` but is addressed inside the body as `[rsp + adjust + 0x28]`, and getting
`adjust` wrong attributes another object's displacements to this one - this walker's own
retraction history. `prologue_adjust` accepts exactly three shapes - `push` (8), `sub rsp,imm`,
and a home-slot save (no movement) - and **refuses** anything else rather than guessing.

**A falsifiable prediction, recorded before the code was written:** `0051F9F0` walks the bank
table writing `[rax-8]`, `[rax]`, `[rax+0xc]` with `rax` at element+8 and stride `0x20`, so
`ChunkedSlotBankEntry` must show `+0x00`, `+0x08`, `+0x14`. It shows exactly those.

**Controls held:** the PTR census and the ARRAY census are both byte-identical, so nothing
existing moved.

**Neither type gains a field, and that is worth saying plainly.** Their rows were already read
by hand and cite the very init sites the census now finds - `0051FA60`, `0051FA68`, `0051FA6E`.
What they gain is a checkable artifact where there was none. Twelfth time the store already
knew, and the first where I checked before writing rather than after.

**Three width disagreements surfaced with the artifacts, and I adjudicated them rather than
leaving them.** All three are COMBINED STORES: an 8-byte write of `-1` covering two adjacent
int32 rows (`bankId`+`minusOneDword04`, `occupancy`+`prevIndex`) and `mov [rax+0xc], rdi`
covering `liveInBank`+`firstSlotIndex`. Marked `WIDTH DELIBERATE` with the reason on the row;
the store is back to its single long-standing mismatch.

### A second defect, found by the same run (OPUS)

The walk counted **multi-byte NOPs as accesses**. `nop dword ptr [rax]` is alignment padding
that happens to encode a memory operand and reads and writes nothing. Measured before fixing:
**60 such rows across 14 committed artifacts**, and exactly **one** offset whose only evidence
was a nop - `ManagerSingleton0209BE80 +0x0`, already declared an unobserved span. **So no field
row has ever rested on one**; the defect was latent, not active. Skipped now at the top of the
instruction loop, which is safe because a nop writes no register either.

I regenerated only the artifact I own (`ActorManagerSlot`, one nop row at `+0x1D0` - my
`recordCountByKind` declaration cites the real `movzx` at `00267B50`, not that nop, so it
stands). **The other 13 artifacts are peers' and are reported, not rewritten.**

### Resume 142 (OPUS) - 59 rows that recorded padding as evidence, deleted from 13 peer artifacts

The generator stopped counting multi-byte NOPs, but 13 artifacts already on disk still carried
them. **Deletion, not regeneration**, and the reason is provenance: those 13 came from several
different generators, so re-running mine over a peer's artifact would change far more than the
nop rows and would silently reattribute who produced it. A nop is not an access under any
generator, so deleting exactly those lines is tool-agnostic.

**Verified after, not assumed:** git reports **+0 added, -59 removed** across the 13, so nothing
but those lines moved; per-file line endings preserved (7 LF, 6 CRLF, and they are genuinely
mixed across the store); `check_census_widths` unchanged at 1837 checked, 627 unchecked, its one
long-standing mismatch; `types_index --validate` 443/3862/0/0.

**The one offset that lost all its evidence** is `ManagerSingleton0209BE80 +0x0`, whose declared
row is `unobservedSpan0000` - already unobserved, and unobserved rows are not width-checked,
which is why the gate's counts did not move at all. **No field row has ever rested on a nop**;
the defect was latent and is now closed before it could be used.

Routed as `OPUS-NOTICE-NOP-ROWS-STRIPPED-FROM-13-CENSUS-ARTIFACTS` so the owners see it here

### Resume 143 (OPUS) - four init chains tested, and the obvious inference was wrong three times

Of the 20 `ctor` columns that name no usable address, six read *"the owning X's
initialisation"* - an embedded child pointing at its parent. The obvious move is to substitute
the parent's declared constructor. **I tested it instead, and it is wrong in three of the four
cases I could check.**

| child | parent's declared ctor | does it reach the child? |
|---|---|---|
| `MovementContext` `+0x120` | `ActorStorageRecord` `00266530` | **YES** - six displacements, record `+0x138..+0x152` |
| `SecondaryContext` `+0x350` | `ActorStorageRecord` `00266530` | **no** - zero inside `+0x350..+0x4D8` |
| `BattleTargetBuffer` `+0x778`/`+0xBC0` | `BattleUnit` `00234480` | **no** - the ctor is 156 bytes, zero inside either range |
| `BattleTargetResultEntry` `+0x988` | `BattleUnit` `00234480` | **no** - zero inside `+0x988..+0xB88` |

The same phrase, *"the owning ActorStorageRecord's initialisation"*, is **accurate for one
sibling and not for the other**. Had I propagated the parent's ctor into all six columns - which
is exactly what "resolve the prose to an address" invites - I would have written three wrong
constructors into the store and they would have looked well-sourced.

`MovementContext` now names `00266530` as **measured**, with the explicit caveat that the six
displacements cover its first `0x32` bytes of `0x230` and nothing was checked about the rest.
The other three carry the negative, which is the more useful half: it stops the next person
making the same substitution.

**For `BattleTargetBuffer` I went one step further and found no initialiser at all.** Across the
2,198-row `BattleUnit` census, `+0x778..+0x980` is touched by 27 functions with almost no writes
and `+0xBC0..+0xDC8` by 9, none dominating the way an initialiser does. Consistent with the
buffer being filled in place by the targeting paths - the account its sibling's column already
gives - but recorded as **not proof of absence**, because a writer reaching it through a base
the census does not model would not appear. The column stays a question rather than becoming a
"none".

### Resume 144 (OPUS) - a fourth addressing form, found because it had already made me wrong

I went to `ActorManagerSlot +0x244` - 64 bytes I had declared **unobserved earlier the same
day** - expecting to confirm it was empty. It is a **second 64-byte bind-zeroed block**, the
twin of `+0x204`: `ActorManager_BindLoadedDefinitionPayload` writes eight qwords at `+0x244`
through `+0x27C`, every one `mov qword ptr [rdi + N], rbx` with `rbx` zeroed at `0026C905`.
Eight qwords is exactly 64 bytes, ending flush where `dword0284` begins.

**Why no census saw it, and it is not the reason the neighbour gives.** The `+0x204` row records
a FOLDED-BASE access - the offset baked into a `lea`'d constant, no displacement to match.
These have ordinary displacements. The problem is the ELEMENT BASE: `lea r14,[rip->0x120000]`
then `lea rdi,[r14 + 0x1f78e10]`, the **image-base-relative idiom**. A route seeded by matching
a direct `lea` of the table address never matches, so the function was never even selected as a
host. **A fourth addressing form**, after the register-held base, the `imul`+`add` computed base
and the operand-folded base.

**The first fix failed, and the failure is what located the bug.** I taught the *walk* to
recognise the idiom and predicted `ActorManagerSlot` would gain the eight offsets. It gained
nothing - because `hosts_for` had already excluded the function. Teaching host discovery as well
took it from **45 offsets to 66**, nothing lost, PTR control byte-identical, and all eight
predicted offsets present.

**Three more of my own unobserved rows fell** to the same run, all writes from the same bind:
`+0x1F8` (dword, zeroed), `+0xC8` and `+0xD0` (qwords, zeroed - and `rbx` was checked by
register-access analysis over the whole 1,330-byte body, written once at `0026C905` and next at
`0026CD8D`, after every store that uses it).

**And one of them is a real semantic field.** `+0x15` is `cmp ebp, 3` / `setne al` /
`mov [rdi+0x15], al` with `ebp` the **slot index** - so the byte is **0 for slot 3 and 1 for
every other slot**. This type's own evidence, written from a different direction, already
records that `World_UpdateSimulationTick` drives slots 0..4 in a loop **and slot 3 separately at
0031411D**. The special-casing was known; this is the flag that encodes it.

`ActorManagerSlot`'s unchecked rows: **22 -> 11**.

### Resume 154 (OPUS) - the 0x28 record has a guard, and my own shape note was wrong hours after writing it

I declared `PendingCompletionQueue01F81248` earlier today and said its four-element `0x28`
record gave *"a shape and no meaning"*. Going back for the meaning found both a mechanism and
an error of mine.

**The error first.** The row said the five bytes are *"each written with a small constant (1 or
2, and the pattern differs between elements - 1,1,1,1 for the first two and 1,2,2,1 for the last
two)"*. The constructor actually writes **`+0x00 = 5` and `+0x01..+0x04 = 1`, uniformly, for
every element** - verified at `001BCBA8-001BCBE0` for element 0 and `001BCC0F-001BCC46` for
element 1. **The census gave me widths and offsets but not values**, and the sample it printed
for `+0x58` happened to be an address-take, so I never saw the `5`. The `1,2,2,1` I attributed
to "the last two elements" is real but written by a **different function**, not the
constructor: the elements are uniform at construction and diverge afterwards.

**And the mechanism explains the offset I could only describe as "the most-read in the type".**
Before each default store the code does:

    mov eax, dword ptr [rcx + 0x1c] / shr eax, 7 / test al, 1 / jne <past the write>

So **`+0x1C` is a flags dword and bit 7 suppresses the default**. The constructor writes
`5,1,1,1,1` and the `1.0f` at `+0x0C` **only into an element whose bit 7 is clear**. That is why
`+0x1C` shows eight reads per element - one before each defaulted store. The "most-read offset"
was a guard all along.

Still not claimed: what the record *is*, or what bit 7 means beyond "do not apply the default".

**The lesson is about the instrument, not the type.** A census artifact records offset, width,
kind and the instruction text - but the summary I read to build the row collapses each offset to
one sample. For a field whose *value* is the evidence, that is not enough, and I wrote a shape
note from it anyway. Reading the constructor took ten minutes and contradicted two of its
clauses.

### Resume 155 (OPUS) - a checker I built, priced, and threw away

After correcting my own shape note I asked whether other rows rest on claims the bytes do not

| version | pairs seen | "mismatches" | what they actually were |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| site + any backtick within 60 chars | 2,259 | **1,772** | mis-pairing, and whitespace inside brackets |
| tight pairing, whitespace-insensitive | 1,141 | 356 | the store omits `ptr`; renders `call 00861EC0` where capstone says `call 0x861ec0` |
| + those two conventions, + substring for partial quotes | 1,141 | **150** | still ~85 % notation: the store's own `rip -> ADDR` resolved-target form, uppercase hex, partial quotes |

style here is *"<function> does `a`, `b`, `c`"*, and no site-to-instruction pairing rule can
distinguish that from *"<site> is `a`"*. A verifier would need to accept any instruction within
the cited function - at which point it no longer checks what it set out to check.

**So I deleted it** rather than leave a gate that reports 150 disagreements which are almost all

ignored unless it says why"*, and I could not make this one say why. Recorded here so the next
person sees the three priced versions before rebuilding it.

*What would still be worth building, and is a different tool:* the error I actually made was a

the census artifact carrying the immediate when a store writes one.

## Resume 161 - the store's last width disagreement was a compiler store-merge - 2026-09-20 (OPUS)

`check_census_widths.py` has carried exactly one unresolved row for weeks:
`BattleMenuWidget2DC0 +0x0098`, declared 2, clean census evidence `{4: 2}`. It is now
dispositioned, and the answer is an **artifact class**, not a measurement.

Both 4-byte lines are the same instruction, `mov dword ptr [rsi + 0x98], r14d`, at `002790E9`
and `00279149`. Reading the disassembly at `002790C0..00279120` settles it in one line:

```
002790E0  xor r14d, r14d
002790E9  mov dword ptr [rsi + 0x98], r14d     <- writes 0 to +0x98 AND +0x9A
002790F7  mov word  ptr [rsi + 0x9c], ax
002790FE  mov word  ptr [rsi + 0x9e], cx
```

**r14d is zero.** One instruction writes zero to two adjacent int16s, which says nothing about
either field's width - writing zero to two fields is the same act however it is split. Eight
bytes later the *same sequence* writes `+0x9C` and `+0x9E` at 16 bits, because those take
distinct computed values (`ax` from `movsx eax, word ptr [r15 + 0x9c]`, `cx` from
`movsx ecx, dx`) and the compiler had nothing to merge. **The 16-bit granularity is proved by
the instructions two bytes away.** Widget's own row carries the identical quartet, with the
matching interpolation bases at `+0x84/+0x86/+0x88/+0x8A`.

The row now carries an earned `WIDTH DELIBERATE` marker naming its own width, so it passes both
`reason_after` and `marker_contradicts`. **Store-wide disagreements: 1 -> 0.**

**The class, stated for reuse:** *a source register zeroed immediately before a store wider than
the declared field is a compiler store-merge, and is never evidence of width - look back for the
`xor reg,reg`.* It is the same kind of census artifact as the `nop word ptr [rax + rax]` padding
already filtered store-wide.

### What this opens, and it cuts the other way (OPUS)

The disagreement checker only fires when a census access is **wider than** the declared field.
The same artifact can act in the opposite direction and leave **no** disagreement to find: a
field DECLARED 4 or 8 bytes because a single wide store was seen, where that store was a merged
zero write and the bytes are really two or more narrower fields. Those rows agree with their
census perfectly and are wrong anyway.

That is worth auditing rather than assuming, and the bounded claim is deliberately weak: such a
row's width rests on **no** information, which is not the same as being wrong. Next.

### Two types whose size is not a multiple of their alignment (OPUS)

`check_alignment.py` reports exactly two, and both are real ABI facts rather than typos.

**`FieldRecord`, size `0x3`, strictest align 2.** Not wrong - **packed**. The stride is proved
by the addressing all three accessors share: `lea rax, [r8 + rcx*2]` then a byte access at
`[rcx + rax + 8|9|0xA]`, which is `i*2 + i = i*3`. Consecutive elements sit 3 bytes apart, so
the `uint16` at `+0x000` lands on an odd address for every other element. x86 permits it; a C
compiler will not emit it without `#pragma pack(1)`. **A reconstruction must declare this type
packed**, or its indexing uses a stride of 4 and every record after the first is wrong.

**`RenderResourceEntryBuffer`, size `0x1C`, strictest align 8.** It holds an 8-byte pointer at
`+0x008`, so its alignment is 8 and any C `sizeof` must be a multiple of 8. **0x1C is not.** Two
readings, and nothing measured chooses between them:

- **(a)** it is really `0x20` with four bytes of tail padding, and the parent's
  `unobservedDword02C` **is** that padding - which would make `RenderResourceEntry` natural,
  since `0x10 + 0x20 = 0x30` lands exactly on the 8-aligned `reference`;
- **(b)** the `size` column means the **occupied span** rather than a `sizeof`, in which case
  `0x1C` is right and the question is about the column, not the type.

**Deliberately not changed.** (a) is tidy, and taking it would consume `unobservedDword02C` - an
unexplained gap - purely to make the layout look complete, which is the one move this charter
rules out. Nothing observed writes `+0x2C`. Recorded instead, because either way a
reconstruction **cannot emit this as a plain C struct at 0x1C**: it must pad to `0x20` or inline
the members.

## Resume 170 - nine "unexplained" strides were one x86 idiom and two array declarations - 2026-09-20 (OPUS)

`check_strided_fields.py` reported **9 indexed scalars with no explanation in their own row**.
All nine are now explained and none was a defect; the checker exits 0 with all 18 accounted for.

**Seven of the nine are one fact.** `ActorManagerSlotEntry` is declared `EMBED ActorManagerSlot
+0x110 stride=0x18 count=4`, and **0x18 = 3 x 8**, so the builder forms it the way x86 forms any
stride that is not a power of two: triple the index, then use a scale-8 operand. Read at
`003DA446..003DA497`:

```
003DA446  lea rdi, [rsi + rsi*2]                          ; rdi = i * 3
003DA471  mov dword ptr [rbx + rdi*8 + 0x110], edx        ; shotIndex
003DA47D  mov dword ptr [rbx + rdi*8 + 0x114], ecx        ; frame
003DA484  mov word  ptr [rbx + rdi*8 + 0x118], ax         ; state
003DA462  mov word  ptr [rbx + rdi*8 + 0x11a], r8w        ; entryNumber
003DA44D  movss     dword ptr [rbx + rdi*8 + 0x11c], xmm2 ; clock
003DA48C  mov dword ptr [rbx + rdi*8 + 0x120], 0x3f800000 ; rate = 1.0f
003DA497  mov byte  ptr [rbx + rdi*8 + 0x124], 0          ; clockRunning
```

Every write lands on a declared offset at the declared base, and the effective element stride is
`3 x 8 = 0x18` exactly. **What the checker measured is the SIB scale byte, not the element
stride** - the same idiom as `FieldRecord`, where `i*2 + i` gives a packed stride of 3.

**The other two are each their own array's element stride.** `AchievementDescriptor` is
`ARRAY 0x00D10460 stride=0x8 count=30` and is 8 bytes, so a scalar inside it indexed at 8 is the
array being walked. `NavigationPathState +0x090` is declared `float[128][2]` over 1,024 bytes,
so an 8-byte step is one XZ pair - which the row already said it holds.

**The checker's own wording is the right note to end on:** *"Exiting 0 because nothing is
UNEXPLAINED - not because nothing was found. A new stride with a silent row fails again."*

`ManagerSub0209BE80_A0D0` is `0x990` with a **2,400-byte** unobserved span at `+0x000` and four
small fields at the tail. The parent census shows `003F80E0` doing
`lea r9, [rcx + 0x960]` then `mov dword ptr [rcx], eax` and `lea rcx, [rcx + 4]` - a
dword-stepping write. Read end to end at `003F80E0..003F8133`:

```
003F80EE  lea r9, [rcx + 0x960]        ; the destination
003F8100  mov dword ptr [rcx], eax     ; eax = 0
003F8105  lea rcx, [rcx + 4]
003F8109  cmp r10d, 4 / jb             ; FOUR dwords cleared
...
003F80E7  movsxd r8, edx / shl r8, 4 / add r8, rax   ; 00D11D80 + edx*16
003F811E  mov ecx, dword ptr [r8]
003F8121  mov dword ptr [r9], ecx
003F8124  add r9, 4 / add r8, 4
003F812E  cmp eax, 4 / jb              ; the SAME four slots, filled
```

So `+0x960..+0x970` is a **4-dword array**, cleared and then loaded from a 16-byte row of the
`.rdata` table at `00D11D80`, selected by the caller's `edx`. `dword0960` - declared PROBABLE
because *"the only accesses here are two 4-byte writes"* - is **slot 0**; the other three were
unobserved only because a census records a loop body once.

**A gated suppression, and it is all-or-nothing rather than a compaction.** `cmp edx, 1` then
`cmp dword ptr [02092730], 4` skips the copy **without advancing `r9`**. Neither value changes
inside the loop, so for row 1 with that global at 4, *nothing* is copied and the array keeps its
zeros.

**The source table, read from the image:** row 0 `{1,1,1,1}`, row 1 `{4,3,2,1}`, rows 2-4
`{4,0,0,0}`, rows 5-6 `{5,0,0,0}`, row 7 `{4,3,6,0}`, row 8 `{4,1,0,0}`. Row 9 reads
`{0x138F,0x64,0x1395,0x64}` - a different shape entirely - so the table is **nine rows** and the
tenth is other data.

**Bounded, and the bound is stated on the row:** the row count is inferred from that change of
shape, **not** from a bound on `edx`. `003F80E0` has **zero `E8` callers** in a whole-`.text`
scan, so nothing found so far bounds the index. And what the four values *mean* is not claimed -
only that they are one array loaded from one row.

**The 2,400-byte span at `+0x000` is untouched.** Nothing censused reads or writes it; the only
access to the object at all is `lea rcx, [rbx + 0xa0d0]` taking its address. It stays UNKNOWN,

## Resume 180 - the procedure I ran by hand three times today is now an instrument - 2026-09-20 (OPUS)

Three open byte ranges closed today by the identical procedure: take an indexed access,
disassemble the function it sits in, read the `cmp` that guards it. `BootSingleton01F7F598
+0x0BE0` (`cmp edx, 0xa`), `ActorStorageRecord +0x0C8` (`cmp r8d, 0x11`),
`ManagerSub0209BE80_5380 +0x342` (`cmp eax, 6`). That does not need a person.

`find_index_bounds.py`: **16,923 indexed accesses examined, 38 with a guarding bound, across 10
types.** Both controls pass and census coverage is printed with every run.

**Two failures on the way, and each taught the rule it enforces.**

- **The guard is rarely on the index register.** v1 required the same register and its own
  positive control refused it: `ActorStorageRecord +0x0C8` indexes with `rsi` while the guard
  is `cmp r8d, 0x11`, because `mov edi, r8d` then `movsxd rsi, edi` carry it across. A forward
  copy chain fixes it.
- **A `cmp` is not a bound unless the branch is an ordering one.** v2 then reported `0xE` for
  that same control, having taken the nearer `cmp edi, 0xe` / **`jne`** — an equality test that
  selects a case. Restricting guards to `ja/jae/jb/jbe/jl/jle/jg/jge` gives `0x11`.
- And a third: a `cmov` on the way to the site is **not** a plain write. `cmovb edi, eax` at
  `00265305` made v3 drop the provenance and find nothing. A conditional move leaves the index
  as *either* the guarded value or a substitute, so the chain survives and the row is marked
  **`[via cmov]`** rather than reported as unconditional.

**What it found** — the largest, each `the accessor admits N`:

| type | offset | index | scale | bound | admits | span |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `BattleTargetBuffer` | `+0x0008` | rax | 8 | 0x20 | 33 | 0x108 |
| `BattleUnit` | `+0x0BC8` | rcx | 8 | 0x20 | 33 | 0x108 |
| `BattleTargetResultEntry` | `+0x0000` | rax | 8 | 0x1F | 32 | 0x100 |
| `BattleUnit` | `+0x0000` | rax | 4 | 0x1F | 32 | 0x80 |
| `ActorStorageRecord` | `+0x00C8` | rsi | 2 | 0x11 | 18 | 0x24 *(via cmov)* |
| `ImageBackedStateBlock` | `+0x0000` | rcx | 4 | 0xB | 12 | 0x30 |
| `CharacterRenderRecord` | `+0x00A0` | rax | 4 | 0x8 | 9 | 0x24 |

`BattleUnit +0x0780`, `+0x0788` and `+0x0988` repeat `BattleTargetBuffer`'s and
`BattleTargetResultEntry`'s bounds at the same sites, which is the embedded child seen through
the parent - the check agreeing with the declared containment rather than finding anything new.

**The caveat is in the tool, not only here: A BOUND IS NOT A LENGTH.** It is the largest index
the code will *form* - an upper bound on what it can reach. A table can be shorter with a
generous guard, or the guard can protect one caller's use of a longer one. The output says *the
accessor admits N* and never *the array has N*. Closing that distance needs a second reading:
the out-of-range path, a count field, or a constructor - which is exactly what the
`BootSingleton` case had when its fallback returned element 9.

## Resume 181 - the bound instrument's first real finding, and it is a question for FABLE - 2026-09-20 (OPUS)

for. Fixing one bug in the tool first, because the comparison exposed it.

**`admits = bound + 1` is wrong for half the branches.** `ja` (exit on >) leaves `<= bound`, so
bound+1 values; **`jae` (exit on >=) leaves `< bound`, so bound**. For a backward loop edge it
inverts again. The rule is now in the file and **all three hand results reproduce under it** -
BootSingleton `jae` 0xa -> 10, ActorStorageRecord `ja` 0x11 -> 18, `_5380` `jb` 6 -> 6. The fix
immediately paid for itself: `CharacterRenderRecord +0x00A0` went from a spurious *admits 9,
0x24* to **8, 0x20**, which is exactly its declared `float[8]`.

| against the declared layout | count |
|---|---:|
| declared size **equals** the admitted span | 2 |
| declared region **larger**, no conflict | 5 |
| **admitted span exceeds the declared row** | **6** |
| no row at that offset (mostly `SavePayload` interiors) | 25 |

00302419  ja 0x3035c0
00302428  movzx ecx, word ptr [rax + rcx*2 + 0x50]
0030242D  mov eax, 0xffff
00302432  cmp cx, ax

## Package 114 - the fourth widget level, and the census that was measuring the wrong register (OPUS)

`OPUS-CENSUS-BATTLE-MENU-WIDGET-2DC0` asked for an accesses.tsv with a control and either
an EMBED child type or a recorded reason there could not be one. **The artifact already
existed and the child type was already declared.** What was open was whether either was
right, and neither entirely was.

### The premise in the task was false, and the instrument is why (OPUS)

The task states that `002778C0` does `mov rsi, rcx` at `002778FC` **"so every `[rsi+N]` in
it is a field"**, and reports 32 displacements with a high-water mark of `0x2DB6`. `rsi`
does not survive the body:

```
002778FC  mov rsi, rcx            ; receiver established
00278701  mov rsi, [rbp - 0x21]   ; RELOADED from a stack slot
00278FD2  add rsi, 0x1600         ; RE-BASED
00278FE3  lea rsi, [rsi + 0x1620] ; re-based again, in a loop that runs twice
```

A flow-sensitive census of the same body reports **30**, not 32. **Two of the five extra
displacements are `lea` operands - instructions that touch no memory at all**, and
recording one as an access is how `0x2C20` and `0x17A8` became "fields". The other three
are first-iteration values of a register the loop re-bases. All five lie inside the two
declared children. `0x2DB6` survives and is still the highest offset the object is seen to
use.

**And the flat shape cannot see the other direction at all.** Thirteen sites reach this
object with the receiver as the **INDEX** register and a multiple of the stride as the
base - `mov ecx, dword ptr [rbx + rsi + 0x5b8]` with `rbx = imul rax, 0x1620`. A base-only
harvest never looks there. Those thirteen are where nine of the child's fifteen offsets
come from.

`gfz-scripts/receiver_flow_census.py` is that census, and it enforces two controls on
itself because both changed the answer: **the recording pass runs after the fixpoint
converges** (recording inside it banks states the loop's back edge later refutes, which
invented four fields), and **every jump table must be supplied** - `002778C0` has four, and
following only the first leaves 140 instructions unvisited.

### The boundary, to the byte (OPUS)

`002778C0` is 9,374 bytes, `002778C0..00279D5E`, 2,061 instructions, clean linear decode,
terminating `ret`. The 194 bytes to the next listed entry are **not an unlisted body**:
they are this function's own switch tables, and they account for the gap exactly -
`00279D5E` 2-byte nop, `00279D60` 14 dword targets, `00279D98` 45 byte indices, pad,
`00279DC8` 2 targets, `00279DD0` 17 indices, pad, `00279DE4` 8 targets, `00279E04` 7
targets, then `00279E20`. Every target lies inside the body; the index tables' maxima are
in range. **2,061 of 2,061 instructions reached.**

### One of the nine seeds is not what the header says it is (OPUS)

`00249C60` is listed as a function "this handler passes the object to in rcx", with 3
calls. There are **13**, and **every one loads rcx with a small integer** - `mov ecx, 5`,
`mov ecx, 0xa`, `mov ecx, r12d`, `lea ecx, [r14 + 3]`. It takes an int. **No row is
affected**, because the emitter attributed nothing to it - which is exactly why a wrong
seed sat in a published header unchallenged. The other eight are confirmed independently.

### Five rows claimed "no access reaches it" over bytes that are read (OPUS)

`BattleMenuChildWidget1620` was declared from a census of its handler `0027AD70` that found
**two** offsets; the same 389 bytes yield **seven**, and the parent's indexed walk adds two
more. So `+0x9C`, `+0x1518`, `+0x1528` each carried a **refuted absence claim**, the
32-byte span at `+0x20` covered the read at `+0x38`, and the 5,232-byte span said "NOTHING
reaching this type touches" over `+0x4C8` and `+0x500`. Sixteen rows became twenty-four.
The refuted sentences were **replaced, not prepended** - a reader skimming must not meet the
false claim first - and each correction quotes the wording it withdraws.

### What the type actually is, and the part that is ownership rather than layout (OPUS)

- **`+0x1510` is OWNED, with both ends of the lifetime in one function.** Built by
  `002D14E0` at `0027AEB1` and stored at `0027AEB9`; attached through `00244960`; and on
  the destroy message `0027ADA3`/`0027ADAA` hands it to the widget teardown `00245020`.
- **`+0x1520` is NOT owned, and is called through.** It comes from the construct message's
  own argument (`mov rax, [rsi+8]`) and is invoked at `0027ADD0`/`0027ADD8` as
  `mov rax,[rcx]; call rax`. **The contrast is in the same function on the same two
  messages**, which is what makes the distinction evidence rather than convention.
- **`+0x1528` is a flags word** - three distinct bits at three distinct sites: bit 17
  gates a message in the child's own handler, the parent clears bit 19 and tests/clears
  bit 21. Which state each bit carries is not claimed.
- **The pair is INDEXED, not merely adjacent.** `word [parent + 0xDA]` selects the
  instance, 19 `imul <reg>, <reg>, 0x1620` sites multiply it, and `0027921C`
  `xor word ptr [rsi + 0xda], 1` **toggles it between 0 and 1** - a proof of the count of
  two that does not go through the two construction calls.
- **The parent's own dtor cell closes.** It read "NOT CLAIMED: whether the release path at
  00245020 reaches either instance". It reaches **both**, at `00279D0F` and `00279D1B`,
  symmetric with the two construct calls. `00245020` is a teardown, not a free: it
  dispatches the object's own proc, walks the child list, and only then tests
  `byte [rdi+0x40] & 0x20` - the bit this store already documents as "the release must not
  free this widget" - to choose between the free at `002482E0` and a flag update.

The two parent rows are no longer `u8[5664]`: **11,328 bytes of byte coverage became a
typed child.** Zero gaps was already true of them and meant nothing.

```
00247570  test rcx,rcx / je ret ; test rdx,rdx ; lea rax,[00915198]
          cmovne rax, rdx ; mov qword ptr [rcx + 0x48], rax
```

`00915198` is **the default arm of a cmovne**. Measured over the graph's **127 callers**,
decoding each body gives **137 call sites**: **97 pass a different table, covering 64
distinct `.rdata` addresses; 2 pass null and take the default; 38 are unresolved by the
method and are scored neither way.** The worked counterexample is this package's own child -
`0027AEE3` passes `00915A80`. The row is corrected; because it is on the base type, the
claim it withdrew applied to every widget in the store.

### Two defects in my own instruments, both caught by their own output (OPUS)

**The control's reference data was retyped by hand.** `WIDGET_DECLARED` was listed from
memory, left out `+0x48`, and the control fired on an offset Widget does declare. It now
reads Widget's rows from the store. *A control whose reference data is hand-entered has an
unmeasured input.*

**A `lea` is not an access**, and my first harvest recorded them as reads - the same defect
I had just written up in someone else's emitter. Address-taken is now its own kind (`a`),
kept because an address handed to a callee is real evidence of a sub-object, but never
counted as a read or a write. Read/write now comes from the operand's own access flags, not
its position, because `test [mem], imm` has the memory operand first and never writes it.

### A latent hazard in the type store's TSVs, and it is not mine alone (OPUS)

`types_index.read_tsv` opens `fields.tsv` in Python's **universal newline** mode. With
`core.autocrlf=true`, a `git checkout` of these LF-stored blobs hands back a **CRLF**
working tree - so every row's last column ends in a CR **that the reader treats as the end
of the line**. It is harmless only while nothing follows it. Append to the last column
without stripping it and the row splits in two:

```
ERROR  fields.tsv references unknown type ' || setter 00247570; 137 call sites ...'
```

The second hazard is the obvious fix being wrong: deciding the terminator **once for the
whole file** and re-applying it rewrote 3,905 lines for a two-row edit, which buries the
change and would sweep an unrelated line ending into a commit. `Tools/work/OPUS/tsv_lines.py`
keeps **each line's own terminator**. Anyone appending to a cell in these files needs both
halves of this.

### Also reported, not edited (OPUS)

`check_census_widths.py` and `check_census_overlap.py` derive their root from
`os.getcwd()`, so both fail or report an empty control when run from the kit directory -
`check_census_overlap` prints "CONTROL FAILED: fewer than two censuses" and exits looking
tidy. This is the defect `kit_paths`' own docstring describes for seventeen other scripts;
these two were not converted. Routed, not changed - they are gates and not mine to touch
mid-package.

### Corroboration nobody arranged (OPUS)

Grepping the handler address **after** the rows were written found

from 7 shared sites.

## Package 115 - both ASTRA contradictions accepted, and one of them was mine twice over (OPUS)

Two P1 contradictions arrived against my own claims while package 114 was being written.
**Both are accepted in full.** Each was verified from the image before agreeing, not taken
on assertion - and in both cases checking made the concession sharper rather than softer.

### The four D3D descriptors: right diagnosis, invented repair (OPUS)

`ASTRA-CONTRA-OPUS-PHYRE-CORRECTED-DESCRIPTOR-IDENTITY`. My answer to their mapping
request had two halves. The **diagnosis** was right - `02CF6678` is a 4-byte MSVC
thread-safe-static guard, not a descriptor. The **repair** was invented: "the object sits
at guard − 0x58" was an arithmetic pattern read off four unrelated `0x60`-stride statics in
`00617E60` and generalised. The real descriptors are in a different family of functions
entirely, and where a guard does pair with a descriptor there, the delta is `0x100`.

| class | registrar | descriptor | the guard that was in the map |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CD3D11_BLEND_DESC` | `00613800` | `02CF6320` | `02CF6678` |
| `CD3D11_DEPTH_STENCIL_DESC` | `00613A30` | `02CF5A80` | `02CF6618` |
| `CD3D11_RASTERIZER_DESC` | `00613E80` | `02CF52C0` | `02CF65B8` |
| `D3D11_RENDER_TARGET_BLEND_DESC` | `00614640` | `02CF5EB0` | `02CF6558` |

**The worse half.** I told ASTRA the image could not say which class is which and proposed
a live read to settle it. Each name is a **literal `.rdata` string** passed to the
constructor, and **this store already held all four sizes and two of their registrar
addresses**. I made an absence claim without searching my own artifacts - the exact failure
this store has a rule against. The live proposal is withdrawn.

**The blast radius, measured over the whole map rather than their four.** Every claimed
descriptor address classified by what the image does with it as `rcx`: reaching a
descriptor constructor (`00632C90`/`00632D80`, found by their own `+0x30`/`+0x38`/`+0x3C`
writes rather than from a list) or a descriptor-shaped consumer (`006388C0`, which reads
`+0x30` as a string; `0063BC00`, which reads `+0xD8`/`+0xFC` and dispatches through `[rcx]`)
proves a descriptor; reaching `_Init_thread_header` proves a guard. **330 of 330 decided:
326 descriptors, 4 guards, 0 undecided.** A first version used only `00632C90` and decided
**15 of 330** - reported, because "only four are wrong" would otherwise have rested on 4.5%
of the population.

**The cause is fixed in the generator, and the obvious repair was worse.** The sweep took
whatever was last `lea`'d into `rcx` at a call to a registrar. Dropping the caller-saved
registers at every call is correct by the ABI and took recovery **from 330 to 315** - it
removed the four wrong answers and **eleven right ones** - and **destroyed parent resolution
entirely, 182 → 0**, because registrars really do hold the descriptor in `rcx` across a
call. The candidate is **tested against the control** instead. After: 330 of 330
descriptors, 182 non-null parents, 181 resolved, both size controls 0 violations.

*One correction back to ASTRA:* their sizes are **hex written bare**. `0x108` is 264, not
108; then 52, 40, 32. Read as decimal every one is wrong - and read as hex all four match
the real Direct3D 11 structure sizes exactly, which is independent corroboration.

### AQ-18: the bytes were in the shipped data all along (OPUS)

`ASTRA-CONTRA-OPUS-AQ18-AQ19-NEGATIVE-INFERENCE`, accepted on both points. The method point
is unarguable: **an all-zero sample is exactly what meaningful storage holding its default
looks like**, so no zero read establishes "dead / reserved / padding". The defect was the
inference, not the reading - and the affected rows never carried it; the routing prose did.

Their second point was the one that paid. The VBF ships **sixteen saves** at
`ps2data/image/ff12/katano/ff12savedataNN.sav`, censused by FABLE on 2026-09-12, and the
save-image page already establishes payload `+0x1044` = image `+0x1244`. So AQ-18's span is
image `0xEF6..0x1200` and was readable offline the whole time. **Across all sixteen: zero
non-zero bytes**, with the area id at `+0x1244` coming back in **nine distinct values** as a
control - a constant there would have meant a silently empty read reported as a clean
negative.

**So AQ-18 is WITHDRAWN, not narrowed** - and not because it is answered. Sixteen samples
are still samples. It is withdrawn because a title-screen read would be a **seventeenth
sample of the same kind**. Standing evidence: three independent offline negatives, no
positive. The row's disposition is deliberately unchanged.

**What would actually decide it** is not another sample but a **write census over the
payload span that resolves the receiver at every store site** - an absence over the code
rather than over a moment. That is offline, so it is mine, and it is on the standing list
rather than in ASTRA's queue. **AQ-19 stays open and unnarrowed**: it has no offline byte
source, and I have not established the container-to-instance walk, so I am not sending one
I cannot prove.

## Package 116 - my own parked finding did not reproduce (OPUS)

`OPUS-FINDING-R2` was **my** measurement, parked on the board for publication. Re-deriving
it before publishing is the whole reason to re-derive, and it did not come back.

| | the parked row | an independently written test |
|---|---|---|
| pages claiming `audit.passes >= 1` | 328 | **385** |
| narrow `/falsif/` heading probe misses | 29 | 31 |
| widening the vocabulary leaves | **4** (a 7x correction) | **30** — it moves by **one** |
| controlled exceptions | 2 | 14 |

**Two scoping differences, neither resolved.** The row says "R2 is 328/330", so it counted
against some 330-row table rather than against every page carrying the frontmatter key —
and **I cannot locate that table**. A rung figure whose denominator cannot be found is not
one I will republish. And the row credits spellings like "Attacked and", "Survived",
"What was attacked" with 25 pages; a regex covering those stems finds them on one. **One of
the two censuses is wrong and I have not established which.**

**What survives in both versions, and it is the part worth keeping: the rung is not
hollow.** 355 of 385 pages that claim a pass carry an attack-family heading *independent of
the counter*. I went looking for R2 to be a gate that measured nothing; it is not one.

**What I did not do is route "the two pages" to their owners**, which was this row's own
completion criterion. That list is downstream of the collapse-to-four I cannot reproduce,
and publishing a defect list I cannot re-derive is worse than publishing none.

### The bigger thing the re-derivation turned up (OPUS)

**`audit.passes` counts passes of several kinds.** The pages with no attack heading are
mostly not delinquent: they are `PARTIAL` (claiming no completion to attack), or their
`last_pass_state` is `reverification-against-current-parent`, or their `last_pass_kind` is
`derivation` or `reproduction`. Those are passes that are not falsifications, and **R2 reads
the bare count and cannot tell them apart**. `§10` is not a usable anchor either — pages
number sections freely — so any test has to be on heading text.

Whether a reverification pass satisfies EVIDENCE-STANDARD §8 decides which of the 14 are
exceptions and which are simply a different kind of pass. **That is not mine to rule on**,
and it is live right now: `FRONTIER-REQ-AUDITSPEC-AUDITED-PROMOTION-SWEEP` is ACTIVE and
promotes on `audit.passes >= 1` *plus* a §10 falsification record. Routed to
SWE2-AUDIT-SPEC as `OPUS-REQ-AUDITSPEC-AUDIT-PASSES-COUNTS-PASSES-OF-SEVERAL-KINDS`, with
both exception lists offered and neither presented as a verdict.

## Package 117 - a third contradiction upheld, this one against my own control (OPUS)

`ASTRA-CONTRA-OPUS-AQ18-ZERO-CASE-VERDICT` is the sharpest of the three ASTRA sent today,
because it is the failure I had spent the session finding in **other people's** instruments.

`aq18_flagpayload_span.py` **printed** its population and control figures and then issued
its negative verdict regardless. Their synthetic run reproduces exactly: fed an empty index
it reports *"expected 16, observed 0"*, *"distinct area ids 0"*, *"0 of 0"*, prints the
negative VERDICT, and **exits 0**.

**A control that is printed but not acted on is not a control**, and a negative verdict
earned by a run that read nothing is worth *less* than no run, because it looks like
evidence. This project's own standing rule is *fail closed on unknown or unresolved*, and I
had not applied it to my own script.

Fixed: exit 2 with **no verdict line** on a population that is not the expected 16, on any
file too short for the span or the control, and on fewer than 2 distinct control values (a
constant area id means the read is not landing in decoded per-file data).
`aq18_negative_controls.py` drives three deliberately broken populations — empty index,
9 of 16, every file truncated to `0x400` — and requires each to refuse. **3 of 3 fire.**
The positive inference is narrowed as asked, and the real run's receipt is now committed
rather than living in a consumer summary: 16 of 16, 9 distinct controls, 0 non-zero, exit 0.

**Their scoping is right and is recorded: this does not show the reported 16-save run was
bad.** The defect was acceptance logic and a missing receipt.

## Package 118 - EXP-130 adopted (OPUS)

`00216660` **is normalize-or-zero and its postcondition differs by path**: the zero path
zeroes all sixteen bytes including `w`, the scale path leaves `w` untouched — so *"the
vector is normalized"* is not one postcondition. **And it leaves a live value in `rax`**
that nothing declares: `_finite`'s `1` on the scale path, `0` on the zero path, bit-exact
both ways, propagated by `NCOPY` as its own exit `rax`, and shown live by the `m-pred-r8d`
mutant. Recorded as an undeclared out-parameter a reimplementation must reproduce — exactly
what a functional test that ignores `rax` never catches.

`dst == src` is safe on `VSUB`/`VADD`/`VSCALE` **by construction** — four components into
`rsp` temporaries, one `movups` commit — so a reimplementation that writes components as it
computes them **is not equivalent**, and a test over non-aliased inputs never sees it.

ORACLE's own scope correction is kept visible rather than absorbed: the predicate cells were
first scoped as `q[0x86AC68]`/`q[0x86AC70]`, int3 padding and code bytes, and the corrected
cells resolve **through the import table**, so `_isnan`/`_finite` are import-proven.

*The edit names no function the page did not already carry*, checked directly against
`functions.tsv`, so no pass-22 neighbour is manufactured.

## Package 119 - EXP-131 adopted, and the eligible set is now empty (OPUS)

`06-Movement-And-Navigation/how-a-unit-finds-its-way-across-the-navigation-mesh.md` is
**FABLE's** account of what the navigation query means, so the adoption took only the
representation and reimplementation side and says so in the section itself. The edit names
**no function the page did not already carry**, checked against `functions.tsv` rather than
asserted — so nothing is manufactured for pass 22.

**Record shapes:** adjacency entries are 2 bytes at `m[cur*deg + slot]`, `deg = w[root+0xA]`;
the entry is a **1-based** edge-record index and `0` means no edge; edge record stride **8**,
`{w va, w vb, b +4, b class@+5, b flag@+6}`; grid candidate record stride **0x22** with the
triangle selector at `+0x14`; cell lists `0xFF`-terminated; walk budget `r13d == 0x80`.
Record 0 of the edge pool is unused padding, which is *why* the index is 1-based — and an
implementation that reads it as 0-based takes the padding record for every first edge and is
**wrong without faulting**.

**Four arithmetic behaviours a port loses silently:** the cell division is a signed `idiv`
truncating **toward zero** where Python's `//` floors, which bites only outside the grid
origin — exactly where a corpus tends not to go; `cvttss2si` on overflow or NaN yields
`0x80000000` rather than raising, so a bad coordinate is rejected downstream and not at the
conversion; `_fdclass` sees the **float**, the caller passing by `movss` with no `cvtss2sd`;
and `ECLASS` sign-extends **asymmetrically** — `dx` for the class table index, `ecx` for the
bit-pair table — so a negative **table entry** returns `0xFFFFFFFF` while a negative
**argument** does not, because `classtab[-1]` ships `0x3F800000`.

ORACLE's scope correction is kept as a **named pattern** rather than absorbed: the BSS cells
were first scoped as root `0x5ADFB0` / BASE pool `0x1FED530`; the true targets are
`0x2AEDFB0` / `0x1F83530`, and standalone tests **read zero** until corrected — a silent
wrong answer, not a failure. Third occurrence of that rip+displacement class in ORACLE's
recent packages, so the page tells the next reader to expect it.

### `receiver_flow_census` produced a confident empty census from a bad extent (OPUS)

Exercising the `--bytes` path I had never run: `receiver_flow_census.py 0x27AD70 --bytes 3`,
on a **389-byte** body, reported *"reached 1 of 1 instructions, 0 distinct receiver
displacements"* and **exited 0**. A clean-looking negative from a run that measured almost
nothing.

That is the same shape `ASTRA-CONTRA-OPUS-AQ18-ZERO-CASE-VERDICT` caught in my AQ-18 script
hours earlier — and I had committed this as a **kit tool for the fleet** while writing a
commit message criticising the pattern. Held to the same standard now, `cb040700c`.

**The extent is the one input this census cannot derive for itself**, and a short one does
not fail — it produces a small, clean, confident answer. Two refusals, exit 1, no result:

- a claimed end that falls **inside an instruction**;
- an extent that **disagrees with the function list**, until `--allow-extent-mismatch` says
  the boundary was re-derived from the bytes.

*The split between them is deliberate.* The function list is **not** an authority — it has
been wrong in this store, which is why the override exists — but a disagreement is a reason
to look rather than to proceed silently. The override waives the **list** check only; a
mid-instruction end is still refused, because that is not a disagreement about where a
function ends, it is an extent that cannot be right.

## Package 121 - the destructor class, a failed test reported as failed, and what the claim actually conflates (OPUS)

Fifteen types assert a destructor that owns no storage. Nobody had tested it. I tried, the
test was the wrong instrument, and **the four results it produced are withdrawn** rather
than kept.

### The test, and why its output is worthless (OPUS)

Sweep `.text`, resolve the `rcx` handed to every call, and ask whether any release path -
`00369860` (PREL, the allocator free), `00245020` (the widget teardown) or `002482E0` (the
free behind it) - is ever called **on** one of the fifteen types' instances.

It reported four types *"consistent with the claim"*. **That result is vacuous.** Its own
control line reads:

```
release-path calls whose rcx resolved to a fixed address: 0
```

**Zero.** The graph lists **74 call sites** into those three paths - 7 + 63 + 4 - and the
sweep resolved **none** of them. A test that resolves nothing reports "no hits" for every
input, including inputs where the claim is false. Four "consistent" verdicts on that basis
are the same green-gate-that-measured-nothing shape as the AQ-18 script ASTRA caught this
morning, and they are withdrawn.

**The diagnosis is structural, not a bug.** Every one of those 74 sites computes its
argument from a runtime base — the two I read directly today are
`lea rcx, [rsi + 0xf0]` / `call 00245020` at `00279D0F` and `00279D1B`. A fixed-address
sweep cannot reach them, and **the types making this claim are precisely the ones whose
address comes from a parent pointer.** The instrument and the population are disjoint by
construction. There was no version of this sweep that would have worked.

### What the class test should have asked, because one type already answers it (OPUS)

The claim is worded *"none independent - embedded storage it does not own"*, and that
sentence **conflates two different conditions**:

1. the object is **never passed to a release path** at all; or
2. it **is** passed, and the release deliberately **does not free** it.

`BattleMenuChildWidget1620` is case **2**, proved today: both instances go to `00245020` at
`00279D0F`/`00279D1B`, and `00245020` null-guards, detaches, dispatches the object's own
proc, walks the child list, and only then tests `byte [rdi+0x40] & 0x20` — *"the release
must not free this widget"* — to choose between the free at `002482E0` and a flag update.
**The teardown runs; the free is gated.** That is a much stronger and more useful statement
than "no destructor", and the other fourteen have not been distinguished at all.

So the real class question is not *"is it ever released?"* but *"which of the two is it, and
for the second kind, what sets the bit?"* — and `002482E0` having only **four** callers
against `00245020`'s **63** is the first evidence that case 2 is the common one.

### What would actually test it (OPUS)

Not a fixed-address sweep. For each type, find the sites that **compute** its address as
parent + offset, and follow that computed pointer into a release path — the manual walk that
settled the widget child. That is a dataflow question over 74 known sites, not a search over
address space, and the site list is already in the graph.

## Package 122 - the release population, censused by argument shape (OPUS)

Having said the class question needs dataflow over the release sites rather than an address
sweep, I ran the bounded first half of it: classify every site by the **shape of the
expression that produces its argument**. That much the sites can answer on their own.

**84 call sites** into the three release paths. *The graph's "74" is caller-callee edges,
not sites* — `002778C0` calls the teardown twice on one edge — so the two figures agree and
neither is wrong.

| shape | sites | what it means |
|---|---:|---|
| `mov rcx, reg` — passthrough | **51** | the object came from the caller; undecidable here |
| `mov rcx, [reg+k]` — stored pointer | **22** | a field owns a separately allocated object; this is its free |
| `lea rcx, [reg+k]` — syntactically embedded | **5** | see below, and **two of them are not embedding at all** |
| unresolved / other | 6 | reported, not assumed |

### The classifier mislabelled two of its own five hits (OPUS)

`EMBEDDED lea [reg+k]` is a **syntactic** shape, and two of the five are a different idiom:
`00369846` and `0036A397` both do `lea rcx, [reg + 0x40]` into **PREL**, whose contract takes
the *payload* while the header sits at `payload − 0x40`. That is the allocator converting
**header to payload**, not an object embedded at `+0x40` in a parent. A shape test cannot
tell those apart and mine did not — recorded rather than quietly dropped, because the same
`+k` that means "sub-object" in a widget means "the other end of the allocator header" here.

**So three genuine embedded-sub-object releases, not five.**

### What the three say about the class (OPUS)

| site | argument | status |
|---|---|---|
| `00279D0F` in `002778C0` | parent `+0xF0` | **proven** `BattleMenuChildWidget1620` instance 0 |
| `00279D1B` in `002778C0` | parent `+0x1710` | **proven** instance 1 |
| `00298613` in `002985D0` | `rbx +0xC0` | **WITHDRAWN — the check I named refutes it.** See below. |

**The third one does not hold, and the check that killed it is the one I said would settle
it.** Sweeping every `00245000` builder call for a registration of `002985D0` finds **none**.
The only registration recovered is `00276D30` at `0027A42D` with `edx = 0x3010` — which is
`BattleMenuPanelWidget3010`'s *already declared* handler, exactly as the store records it.

So `002985D0` is not that type's handler, and the sole basis for the identification was that
`+0xC0` matched the route offset. **That is precisely what this store forbids**: matching
offsets do not prove identical types. `rbx` there is some other object that also has a
widget at `+0xC0`; the function's widget-message shape and its `00245020` call make it *a*
widget releaser, not *that* one.

**Two types settled, not three.** The correction cost one sweep and is recorded because the
lead was published in `bfdffc0ff` before it was tested.

The third arrives through the **guarded-release idiom**: `lea rcx,[rbx+0xC0]` /
`call 00273A20` / `cmp eax, 1` / `jne` / `lea rcx,[rbx+0xC0]` / `call 00245020` — the guard
decides, and only then does the teardown run.

### And the non-contiguity is explained — it is not a property of MLOAD (OPUS)

Reading the whole region at 16-byte stride instead of only the four cells MLOAD touches:

| cell | value | | readers (rip-relative census) |
|---|---|---|---:|
| `0x8C5F80` | `[ 1, 0, 0, 0]` | **+X**, MLOAD row0 | 49 sites / 42 functions |
| `0x8C5F90` | `[ 0, 1, 0, 0]` | **+Y**, MLOAD row1 | 45 / 39 |
| `0x8C5FA0` | `[ 0,-1, 0, 0]` | **−Y**, *skipped* | **1 / 1** |
| `0x8C5FB0` | `[ 0, 0, 1, 0]` | **+Z**, MLOAD row2 | 47 / 42 |
| `0x8C5FC0` | `[ 0, 0,-1, 0]` | **−Z**, *skipped* | **3 / 3** |
| `0x8C5FD0` | `[ 0, 0, 0, 1]` | **W**, MLOAD row3 | **90 / 73** |

It is a **signed axis-basis bank**, and the two cells MLOAD steps over are the **negative
axes** — not padding, not a stride oddity. The usage census splits the same way the geometry
does: the positive axes and W are read by dozens of functions each, the negatives by one and
three. The W row is the most-read constant of the six, which is what a homogeneous row
should be.

**Why this is worth more than the original phrasing.** *"Non-contiguous cells"* reads as an
oddity of MLOAD and invites a port to hard-code four scattered addresses. The bank reading
says the opposite: this is **shared engine-wide constant storage**, identity is simply the
subset `{+X, +Y, +Z, W}`, and MLOAD is not reaching around a hole — it is selecting the rows
it wants from a table that also serves everyone else. **A port should carry the bank, not
the four addresses.** Routed to ORACLE as
`OPUS-NOTICE-ORACLE-MLOAD-IS-NOT-READING-A-NON-CONTIGUOUS-MATRIX-IT-IS-PICKING-FROM-AN-AXIS-BANK`.

## Package 126 - why the destructor class was never testable, and it is not anyone's oversight (OPUS)

The class question — do the 15 types asserting *"no independent storage"* ever get released —
now has a structural answer, and it explains every failed attempt at it including mine.

### Tracing the passthrough sites (OPUS)

Of the 84 release call sites, 51 were `mov rcx, reg` passthrough. Traced to an origin inside
their own function — **40 resolved under a stricter shape filter than the earlier count used,
and the 40 vs 51 difference is the filter, not a loss**:

| origin | sites | |
|---|---:|---|
| unresolved | 16 | reported, not guessed |
| **ARG0** | **15** | the caller decides; the question moves up a level |
| FIELD | 7 | a field owns it — the same answer as the 22 stored-pointer sites |
| EMBEDDED | 1 | a sub-object at a fixed offset |
| RETURN | 1 | a callee produced it |

### The finding: **10 of the 14 ARG0 releasers have ZERO callers in the graph** (OPUS)

A function that releases its own argument and has no callers is not dead — it is reached
**indirectly**. Tested rather than assumed, by sweeping every `00245000` builder call for a
registration of each:

| releaser | registered at | in | object size |
|---|---|---|---|
| `00279E20` | `002766E0` | `00276650` | **`0x61F0`** |
| `0027AA70` | `0027A392` | `00279E20` | **`0x4A0`** |
| `0029A0A0` | `0029BBDA` | `0029BB40` | **`0x160`** |
| `003CA310` | `003CA8DC` | `003CA860` | **`0x4A0`** |

Four of fourteen are **registered widget handlers**, and `00279E20` at `0x61F0` is the exact
widget this session opened on — the board task's own chain says *"002766E0 builds the 0x61F0
widget at singleton+0xAB30 with handler 00279E20"*. The remaining ten are not registered by
that route and are still unexplained.

**So the release layer for widget-family types is entered through handler registration and
indirect dispatch.** `00245020` itself does `mov rax, qword ptr [rdi]` / `call rax` — it
dispatches the object's own proc. **A static call graph structurally cannot see that edge**,
which is why:

- my fixed-address sweep resolved **0 of 84** release arguments — every one comes from a
  runtime base;
- the call-graph census shows these releasers with **no callers at all**;
- and the class has sat untested — *not* through anyone's oversight, but because the obvious
  instrument is blind to the mechanism by construction.

**That is the honest answer to the class question**, and it is worth more than a verdict on
fifteen rows: *"is it ever released?"* cannot be settled from the call graph for any type
whose release runs through a registered handler. It needs the registration table, which is
recoverable — the sweep above is it.

### Two undeclared widget types fell out, with sized-by-argument evidence (OPUS)

`0029A0A0` for a **`0x160`** one. Each has the shape the store's ctype rule asks for — an

## Package 127 - the fourteen releasers are fully accounted for, and the split is exact (OPUS)

The previous package left ten of the fourteen ARG0 releasers unexplained. They are explained,
and the answer is cleaner than expected.

**Two places a function's address can be taken, both searched:** `lea reg, [rip + d]`
resolving to it (a registration or callback argument), and an 8-byte-aligned qword anywhere in
the image whose value *is* the address (a vtable or dispatch-table slot).

| | direct callers | address taken | count |
|---|---|---|---|
| **INDIRECT only** | 0 | yes | **11** |
| **DIRECT only** | ≥1 | no | **3** |
| both | | | **0** |
| neither | | | **0** |

**Complementary and complete — all 14, no overlap, no residue.** A releaser is reached either
by a direct call *or* by address-taken registration, never both and never neither. That is a
much stronger statement than "some are indirect", and it is the kind of result that is worth
checking precisely rather than eyeballing: the three with no address taken are exactly the
three that have callers.

**Not one of the fourteen appears in a data slot.** Zero vtable entries, zero dispatch-table
entries. **The widget system registers its handlers by ARGUMENT** — passed in `r8` to
`00245000` — not through a table of function pointers. That is why a data-section scan for
handlers finds nothing and why the registration sweep is the instrument that works.

So the picture from Package 126 holds and is now quantified: **11 of 14 releasers are
invisible to the call graph**, and the mechanism is argument-passed registration reached
through `00245020`'s `mov rax, [rdi]` / `call rax`.

*What is still not claimed:* `INDIRECT only` says the address is taken, not that the taking
site is a handler registration — four are proven registrations via `00245000`, the other seven
are address-taken by some site this pass did not classify. And "neither" would not have meant
dead: a computed jump is invisible to both searches. The bucket is empty, so the question
does not arise, but the limit is recorded because it would have mattered had it not been.
