## Package 128 - there are TWO registrars, and the second one is the pool (OPUS)

Following the address forward from each `lea` to whatever consumes it — the step named at the
end of Package 127 — resolves **all eleven** indirect releasers, with **nothing unclassified**:

| registrar | argument | releasers |
|---|---|---:|
| `00245000` | **arg2** (`r8`) | **4** — the widget builder already known |
| `00244F50` | **arg1** (`rdx`) | **7** — a second registrar, not previously identified |

`00229590`, `00253780`, `002B7590`, `002BA700`, `0037F4D0`, `003CB650` and `0057A620` all reach
`00244F50` with their address in `rdx`.

### `00244F50` is the FIXED-POOL widget allocator (OPUS)

Read from the bytes:

```
00244F64  mov rsi, r8
00244F67  mov rbp, rdx            ; arg1 = THE HANDLER
00244F6A  mov edi, ecx            ; arg0 = a size
00244F6C  test ecx, ecx
00244F70  mov edi, 0xC0           ; DEFAULT SIZE 0xC0 when arg0 is zero
00244F77  cmp ecx, 0x120
00244F7D  ja  0x244FB0            ; REJECTED above 0x120
00244F7F  mov rbx, [0208EA58]     ; a pool pointer in .data
00244F90  test dword [rbx + 0x40], 0x4000
```

`[rbx+0x40]` is **Widget's own `flags`**, and `CONTRACT-widget-object.md` already defines that
bit: *"bit `0x4000` cleared and then re-set from the 5th argument — `(pooled & 1) << 14`, i.e.
**bit 14 means 'this object came out of the fixed pool'**"*. So the scan walks the pool looking
at each entry's pool bit. **The contract had the bit; nothing had the allocator.**

### Which splits the destructor class properly (OPUS)

*"No independent storage"* has been one label over **two different lifetimes**:

| | storage belongs to | registrar | how the release knows |
|---|---|---|---|
| **embedded** | the parent object | `00245000`, in place | the parent tears it down (`00279D0F`/`00279D1B`) |
| **pooled** | the fixed pool at `*(0208EA58)` | `00244F50`, size ≤ `0x120`, default `0xC0` | **flags bit 14** records the origin |

And these are **two different bits of the same field doing two different lifetime jobs**:
`00245020`'s teardown tests `byte [rdi+0x40] & 0x20` — *"the release must not free this
widget"* — to choose between the free at `002482E0` and a flag update, while **bit 14** records
that the storage came from the pool. One decides whether to free; the other records where it
came from.

**That is the answer the class was actually asking for.** Not "is it ever released" — every one
is — but *whose storage is it*, and the store has been recording two mechanisms under one

## Package 130 - PREL's callers, censused completely, and what it says about the twelve (OPUS)

The twelve non-widget types in the destructor class each need parent-ownership evidence, which
is twelve investigations. **One question covers all twelve at once and has a complete
denominator**: the widget teardown is irrelevant to them, so if a plain embedded record were
ever separately freed it would go through **PREL `00369860`**, the allocator's free — and PREL
has **seven** callers, small enough to examine entirely rather than sample.

| caller | size | reaches PREL by |
|---|---:|---|
| `003697F0` | 13 B | **tail `jmp`** — `test rcx,rcx / je ret / xor edx,edx / jmp PREL` |
| `00369800` | 85 B | **tail `jmp`** at `00369846` |
| `0036A2A0` | 495 B | `call` at `0036A397`, `rcx <- lea rcx,[rbp+0x40]` |
| `0036B980` | 727 B | `call` at `0036BC3B`, `rcx <- mov rcx, rsi` |
| `0036C4B0` | 229 B | `call` at `0036C541`, `rcx <- mov rcx, rsi` |
| `0036CB00` | 1353 B | `call` at `0036D013`, `rcx <- mov rcx, r15` |
| `0036D050` | 269 B | `call` at `0036D069`, `rcx <- mov rcx, r8` |

**5 call sites and 2 tail jumps — 7 of 7 accounted for.** The two that a `call`-only scan
missed are the reason to look: a tail `jmp` is a call the caller does not return from, and a
census that reports "5 sites across 7 callers" without explaining the gap has an unexamined
remainder it is not admitting to.

**Every one of the seven lies inside the allocator family**, `003697F0`–`0036D050`. **Nothing
outside it calls PREL at all.**

### What that does and does not settle for the twelve (OPUS)

It **removes the mechanism that would most obviously refute them**: a plain embedded record
cannot be handed to the allocator's free by game-side code, because game-side code never
reaches that path — the only entries are the allocator's own internals, and those free whole
blocks rather than sub-records. That is a complete-denominator negative, not a sample.

It does **not** prove the twelve are never separately released. Another mechanism could exist
that this does not cover, and `003697F0` — a **null-guarded forwarder**, `PREL(rcx, 0)`, the
shape of a public `free(ptr)` — is exactly where one would look next, since a forwarder's own
callers are a different population from PREL's.

**So the class stands as: 3 widget types embedded and proven; 12 plain records whose most
likely refutation is now ruled out over a complete population, and whose positive proof is
still per-parent.** That is a real advance on "untested as a class" and it is not a closure.

## Package 138 - the panel slot is constructed twice, and I filed it as a question (OPUS)

The releaser census left three undeclared widget handlers with construction-argument extents —
`0027AA70` and `003CA310` at `0x4A0`, `0029A0A0` at `0x160`. Proving one properly, the way
`BattleMenuChildWidget1620` was proven, is consequential structure rather than declaration
volume, so it is work the directive favours. Reading `0027AA70`'s registration turned up
something else.

**Two in-place constructions, in one function, at the same base expression:**

```
0027A392   lea r8,[0027AA70] / mov edx,0x4a0  / shr rcx,1 / and ecx,r15d
           imul rax,rcx,0x3010 / lea rcx,[rbx+0xc0] / add rcx,rax / call 00245000
0027A42D   lea r8,[00276D30] / mov edx,0x3010 / shr ecx,1 / and ecx,r15d
           imul rax,rcx,0x3010 / lea rcx,[rbx+0xc0] / add rcx,rax / call 00245000
```

Identical apart from **size and handler**. The base is `rbx + 0xC0 + index * 0x3010` at both,
and both derive the index from the same field — `0027A370` writes `ecx` to `[rbx+0x61cc]`,
`0027A397` reads it back, same `r15d` mask, same shift by one. On that reading **the same slot
gets a `0x4A0` construction and then a `0x3010` one**, and the store records only the second:
`BattleMenuPanelWidget3010`'s `ctor` cites `0027A42D` alone.

### Filed as a question, not answered (OPUS)

`OPUS-QUESTION-THE-PANEL-SLOT-IS-CONSTRUCTED-TWICE-WITH-TWO-SIZES`. **No row is changed on this
evidence**, because the thing that would settle it is exactly what I have not done: the two
shifts differ in width (`shr rcx,1` against `shr ecx,1`) and I traced neither operand to its
source. **If a different value reaches them, the two constructions hit different slots and the
question dissolves entirely.** That trace is the first step and it is named as such.

*Three readings, none preferred*: a first phase of the same object; a base-class construction
later widened; or a distinct type that merely shares the slot's base address. The third is the
one this store explicitly forbids assuming either way — **sharing a base address is not
identity** — which is why the `0x4A0` is not declared here on the strength of a size and a
handler.

**This is the right shape for a last finding**: it touches a type I declared earlier today, it
would have been easy to write up as "a new 0x4A0 widget type", and the evidence does not carry
that. What it carries is a discrepancy worth someone's attention, with the one measurement that
decides it named.

## Package 139 - the question answered the same session it was filed, and my premise was wrong (OPUS)

Package 138 filed `OPUS-QUESTION-THE-PANEL-SLOT-IS-CONSTRUCTED-TWICE-WITH-TWO-SIZES` and named
the deciding measurement as *"the first thing to do and it is not done"*. It is done, and it
**refutes the question's own framing**.

### The two sites never both run (OPUS)

- Site 2's block at `0027A3E7` is entered **only** by a `je` from `0027A312`.
- Site 1's block ends at `0027A3C4` with `jmp 0027A704` — the common exit. **It does not fall
  through.**

So on any single pass through `00279E20` **at most one of the two constructions runs**. They
are alternative message cases, not sequential phases of one slot. *"The same slot gets a `0x4A0`
construction and then a `0x3010` one"* is wrong.

My backward register-tracer had suggested otherwise, and I did not trust it for the decisive
claim — it is loose enough to pick up an instruction that is not in the dependency chain, and
reading the straight-line code between the two sites is what settled it. **A loose instrument
is fine for finding a lead and not for closing one.**

### What survives, and it is better than the question (OPUS)

Site 1's path, immediately after its construct call, reads `[rbx+0x61cc]`, **toggles bit 1**
with the `not / xor / and 2 / xor` idiom at `0027A3A0..0027A3A9`, and stores it back at
`0027A3AE`. That is the **same page-flip shape** as `xor word ptr [rsi+0xda], 1` at `0027921C`
in `BattleMenuWidget2DC0`, found this morning — a 0/1 selector flipped after use. So **bit 1 of
`+0x61CC` selects which of the two `0x3010` panel slots is current**, and one message case
advances it.

**`BattleMenuPanelWidget3010` is not missing a construction phase.** Its `ctor` citing
`0027A42D` alone is correct for what that type is, and the declaration stands unchanged.

*Still not declared*: the `0x4A0`. It now looks like the third of the three readings — a
distinct object sharing a slot's base address — which is exactly the case this store forbids
concluding **from** a shared base address. It has a size from a construction argument and a
registered handler, which is the entry ticket; it does not have its receiver proven through the
construction chain, and that is what a declaration needs. It stays a candidate alongside
`003CA310` and `0029A0A0`.

## Package 140 - two node types that share a size and an offset set and are not the same type (OPUS)

The parked census `OPUS-NOTE-ORDERED-CONTAINER-FAMILY-CENSUS` asked for a page and got one on
2026-09-15. Checking it before closing the row: **every element of the parked note is on that
page**, including the caller-subsystem table it said whoever wrote the page must account for in
the same edit. Nothing was lost in the parking. **What nobody had done was declare the type the
census derived** - the canonical store held no row for either red-black node layout in this image.

### Measured here, not adopted (OPUS)

Six EASTL bodies and six MSVC ones decoded linearly from their listed entries, each extent
**refused unless the last instruction ends exactly on it**: 1,741 bytes / 521 instructions for the
EASTL family, which reproduces the page's corrected figure from the other side.

`EastlRbTreeNodeBase` and `MsvcTreeNodeHeader`, `0x20` each, 11 field rows.

**The size, the four principal offsets and even the `0`=red/`1`=black colour encoding agree, and
three of the four offsets mean different things.** That is the store's own rule - a shared offset
set is not identity - and it had no worked example until now.

| | EASTL | MSVC |
|---|---|---|
| `+0x00` | `mpNodeRight` | `_Left` |
| `+0x08` | `mpNodeLeft` | **`_Parent`** |
| `+0x10` | **`mpNodeParent`** | `_Right` |
| `+0x18` | `mColor` | `_Color` |
| `+0x19` | *(pad)* | **`_Isnil`** |

**The parent, from the mirror-rotation invariant rather than from a library header.** A rotation
exchanges two children and reparents three nodes, so across a mirror pair the offset written the
**same number of times in both directions** is the parent. EASTL `0016D780`/`0016D7E0`: `+0x10`
five and five, children 2/4 and 4/2. MSVC, on **both** pairs: `+0x08` six and six.

**MSVC's parent has two further lines, so it does not rest on one instrument** - the insert's own
store `00712FA3 mov [r11+8], r9` on the node it received as its fifth argument, and the descent
`0070D360`, which climbs no parent at all and so cannot contradict it.

**Child order is opposite and falls out of the walkers.** `0016D6D0` is the successor, so EASTL's
`+0x00` is the RIGHT child; `0070D360` is a `lower_bound` that descends `[node+0]` when the node's
key is at or above the search key, so MSVC's `+0x00` is `_Left`.

**The `+0x19` discriminator re-run as a control rather than quoted:** zero operands at that
displacement across all six EASTL bodies, any width, any mnemonic, against 1/1/1/1/4/18 reads in
the six MSVC ones.

**The extent comes from the other side, which a byte width could not settle.** `FUN_00199db0` asks
its allocator for `0x28` at `00199E70`, takes the payload at `add rax,0x20` and stores an 8-byte
key there - so the EASTL header ends where the payload begins. For MSVC the payload offset is
measured twice, at `0070D360` (key `+0x20`, mapped value `+0x28`) and at the tidy `0071F3A0`. Both
tail pads are therefore **derived from a measured neighbour**, not from an alignment rule alone.

**Lifetime is one chain on the EASTL side:** allocation (`00199E70`), receiver (the same block
passed in `rcx` at `00199E8B`) and initialisation (`0016D840`'s first four stores - parent from the
argument, both children null, colour RED) read end to end. The family has no `free` at all; its
entire callee set is the two rotations. The MSVC `allocation_site` is `UNRESOLVED` and **states its
question**: the release is read, the acquisition is not, and a `max_size` constant is a size rather
than a site.

**One identification is not a fingerprint at all.** `00712F89` loads the string
`map/set<T> too long` - MSVC `<xtree>`'s own `_Xlength_error` text, the image naming the library.

**Deliberately L1.** Toolchain code, explicitly not the game's; marking it L2 would move a
game-type-recovery figure it does not touch.

**`count=2` on `BattleMenuPanelWidget3010` was an arithmetic corroboration and is now direct.**
`00279E20` **enumerates the array** at `0027A1B0..0027A1D2` - same base expression as the
construction sites, `imul rcx, rax, 0x3010` / `add rcx, 0xc0` / `add rcx, rbx`, walked with a
literal `cmp edi, 2 / jb` - and exits into `lea rcx,[rbx+0x60e0]`, so **the array's end is measured
from both sides in consecutive instructions**. That also decides
`OPUS-CONTRA-AB30-PANELS-DESCRIBED-TWICE` **in favour of the embed**: the offset `+0xC0` is right,
so the parent reaches into the child's interior, and `ManagerSub0209BE80_AB30`'s field map still

### The publish went wrong, and the first cause was mine (OPUS)

I staged five paths with a raw `git add` and committed. The commit reported *no changes added* and
`HEAD` had moved: **`23219ee2f SWE2-CONTRACT: resume block to b0e4e2bab` carries my five files.**
The next `team.py apply` printed the rule I had broken - *publish document changes with
`publish_paths.sh <msg> <path>...`, never `git add` of shared or unstaged-by-you paths*.

**`git add` writes the repository's index, and every agent in this worktree shares it.**
`publish_paths.sh` exists for exactly this: it seeds a **private** index from `HEAD` through
`GIT_INDEX_FILE` and adds only the named paths, so a peer's staged work cannot be swept in *and
your own cannot leak out*. Had I used it, the commit would have been mine.

Nothing needs undoing - the content landed intact and the store validates - so the notice I filed
against SWE2-CONTRACT was **claimed back and corrected by its author before anyone acted on it**.
The cost is one misleading `git log --oneline` line, which is why the package is recorded here.

FABLE's ruling asked for `check_embed_overlap.py` to be *in the publish gates, not in a one-off*.

### The runner appends an argument seventeen checkers reject (OPUS)

`run_gates.py` passes the corpus path as a **positional**. Seventeen store checkers take `--store`,
`--exe` or nothing, so they die on an argparse error and exit 2. The report then files them under
*NOT IN THE BASELINE (new checker, or baseline not refreshed)* — **where a genuine red and a
mis-invocation are indistinguishable** — and `--adopt-new` deliberately refuses to adopt a red
unless it is named, so they could never enter the baseline by themselves.

Measured: **all seventeen exit 2 under the runner and none of them takes a positional.** Run bare,
**fourteen exit 0 and three exit 1 with findings nobody had seen.**

That is the exact failure the runner's own docstring exists to fix — *"Nothing was broken. Nobody
was looking."* — and the same lesson is already recorded **twice** in that very table, for
`check_contract_runtime_links` and for `check_publish_neighbours` / `check_literal_base_access`.
This is seventeen more of the same class. All seventeen are moved out of the corpus-positional
default; the three that exit 1 are adopted as accepted debt **by name**, because recording a red
as accepted is a decision somebody has to make on purpose.

### Two of those findings are not findings, and the store now says so (OPUS)

`check_alignment`'s tail-padding pass reports two types whose size is not a multiple of their
strictest member alignment. Both are **expected**, and left alone both would report forever, which
is how a checker teaches people to ignore it.

- **`FieldRecord`**, size `0x3`, strictest align 2. Its own route answers it: `PARRAY 0x02ADD100+0x8
  stride=0x3`. The stride is **measured from the indexing arithmetic**, not inferred from a C
  struct's padding, and its fields are named `packedFlags` and `packedOptions`. No padding exists
  to find.
- **`RenderResourceEntryBuffer`**, size `0x1C`, strictest align 8. **The four bytes are the
  parent's, and the parent declares them**: this type is `EMBED RenderResourceEntry +0x10`, the
  parent's row for it is `bufferDescriptor` at `+0x10` with width 28, and the next parent row is
  `unobservedDword02C` at `+0x2C`. An embedded region's extent is the span between its neighbours;
  inventing a tail pad here would take four bytes from a row that already has them.

### A lead that dissolved, recorded because it cost real time (OPUS)

A sweep of every `*accesses.tsv` reported **1,279 malformed lines**. It looked like a data-quality
defect in registered censuses.

**It was my sweep that was wrong.** In eleven of the thirteen files the number was *exactly* that
file's own comment-header count — `clean()` counts a `#` line as a malformed row. The other two,
`formula-scratch-block-accesses.tsv` (912) and `locomotion-angle-accesses.tsv` (307), are a
**different schema**: the first is the address-keyed catalogue `clean_static()` reads correctly and
which the tool's own docstring describes at length; the second is keyed `ctx+0x0` and is cited by
exactly two `BattleUnit` rows, both of which have the registered census to check them.

`clean()` now counts comments separately, so the tally means broken rows again and the next person
does not spend the same hour. **Nothing was wrong with the store.**

### Two chains, and one of them is now a route to a static root (OPUS)

While the lock was held I finished what package 142 started. A whole-image census of `02B47758` —
every listed body decoded, every RIP-relative operand resolved — finds **exactly two writers and
seven readers**, which is the shape a lazy singleton *must* have and is evidence rather than an
assumption:

- **writer 1**, the getter `003CA280`: load, test, build-if-null through `00244F50(0xAA0,
  handler 003CA860)`, store;
- **writer 2**, the releaser `003CA2B0`, 37 bytes and perfectly symmetric: load, null-check,
  `call 00244F00` — the pool **release**, counterpart of the `00244F50` that made it — then zero
  the cell.

So the routes compose to a static root the way this store's grammar asks: the `0xAA0` widget is
`PTR 0x02B47758`, and the `0x4A0` is `EMBED <it> +0x5F0`, built once under the liveness latch.

I hand-decoded `00299090`'s tables to check `resolve_switch_arms.py` on a second case. **My hand

## Package 144 - the two pane widgets declared, and the store's last width mismatch closed (OPUS)

Packages 142 and 143 read the chain and emitted the censuses; this writes the rows.
**`PaneListWidget0B68` and `PaneSlotWidget0160`**, 65 field rows, tiling `0xB68` and `0x160`
exactly.

### Built from the census, not transcribed (OPUS)

Every width is the one `check_census_widths.clean()` reports for that displacement - **the same
function the gate uses to compare a declared row against its evidence** - so a row cannot disagree
with the census it came from. The builder asserts the tiling sums to the declared extent before it
writes anything, and refuses on an overlap or a ctype whose width contradicts the census.

**The parent is a widget with four child widgets.** `002964D0` takes a `0xB68` slot from the widget
pool through `00244F50` at `00296502`, with `0029BE50` in `rdx` - the pool allocator's handler
argument, exactly as `r8` is the in-place constructor's - sets bit 15 of `+0x40` when `002544B0`
returns 1, and returns it. Its four slots at `+0x240` stride `0x160` are **not** built there: the
handler's slot walk builds them one at a time, only when the matching request byte says so.

| | |
|---|---|
| `+0x240` | `paneSlots0240`, `PaneSlotWidget0160[4]`, 1,408 bytes |
| `+0xB44` | `slotRequest`, `uint8[4]` - **one request byte per slot** |
| `+0xB48` | a pane INDEX, not a flag: both reads sign-extend it into `0035BB20`'s argument |
| `+0xB43` | written once and immediately used as the index of the handler's **second** jump table |

**`+0xB44` is the only field on the type reached with the index in a register** rather than as a
displacement - `[rsi + r15 + 0xB44]`, `rsi` the slot index - which is why a displacement-keyed
census alone would have missed it. Four bytes because the walk is bounded by `cmp edi, 4`, the same
bound as the array, and `0xB44 + 4 = 0xB48` is the next evidenced offset.

**The child knows its parent.** `+0x120` is `owner`, `PaneListWidget0B68*`, written by the
construction itself at `0029BBE8` on the object `00245000` has just returned. Nine of its thirty
offsets are Widget's own header and take Widget's names.

### The store's last width mismatch, and it was mine (OPUS)

`check_census_widths` reported exactly **one** MISMATCH across 3,989 field rows, and it was
`PaneSlotWidget0160 +0x40 declared 4, clean evidence {1: 2}` - my own new row.

The two accesses are `test byte ptr [rbp + 0x40], 2`, twice. **Bit tests of the low byte of
Widget's flag word, not evidence of a narrower field.** Widget declares `+0x40` as a `uint32` on
its own evidence - `or 0x80A` at construction, bit 17 from the global `0208ED5C`, bit 14 meaning
the storage came from the fixed pool - and this type *is* a widget. Narrowing the row because this
subclass's handler only ever tests bit 1 would contradict the base type on the strength of an
instruction encoding.

So the row takes the store's **earned** `WIDTH DELIBERATE` exemption, which requires a real reason
and refuses one that names a width the row does not declare. **Zero mismatches store-wide.**

### And the reader had to be fixed twice for the same reason (OPUS)

`clean()` skips line 0 as the header. These census files open with a `#` preamble, so the **real**
column header sits further down - and landed in `census_malformed` with everything else. Package
143 separated the comments; this separates the header. The tally means broken rows again, and the
declaration builder refuses outright on a non-zero malformed count, which is how the second half
was found at all.

## Package 145 - the singleton and its three children, and a checker that corrected itself twice (OPUS)

### The 02B47758 singleton, declared with its whole composition (OPUS)

Four types, 40 field rows. `WidgetSingleton02B47758` at `0xAA0`, and the three child widgets its
handler builds in a **contiguous run**:

| offset | extent | handler | site |
|---|---|---|---|
| `+0x2A0` | `0x1C0` | `003CAB00` | `003CA92B` |
| `+0x460` | `0x190` | `003CAE00` | `003CAA79` |
| `+0x5F0` | `0x4A0` | `003CA310` | `003CA8DC` |

**The arithmetic closes four times and none of it is assumed**: `0x2A0+0x1C0 = 0x460`,
`0x460+0x190 = 0x5F0`, `0x5F0+0x4A0 = 0xA90`, and **`+0xA90` is an evidenced field** of the parent
- four read/write sites - so the run's end is marked by evidence rather than by the last extent.

**Route to a static root, with a teardown.** `PTR 0x02B47758`. A whole-image census of that cell -
every listed body decoded, every RIP-relative operand resolved - finds **exactly two writers and
seven readers**: the getter `003CA280` (load, test, build-if-null through
`00244F50(0xAA0, handler 003CA860)`, store) and the releaser `003CA2B0`, 37 bytes and perfectly
symmetric - load, null-check, `call 00244F00`, the widget pool **release** that is the counterpart
of the `00244F50` that made it, then zero the cell.

### The cross-check that makes the composition more than arithmetic (OPUS)

**Two of the parent's own censused displacements are its child's interior**, and the child's own
census names them at exactly the right offsets:

- parent `+0x6B0` = `child05F0 +0xC0`, address-taken in **both** censuses;
- parent `+0xA80` = `child05F0 +0x490`, read and written in **both**.

Under rule 0 neither gets a parent row. The child declares `+0x490`; `+0xC0` is address-taken only
and a `lea` gives no width, so nothing is declared on it at either level. **Two independent
censuses, run against two different receivers, agreeing on where the same bytes are.**

**The interiors are sparse and the rows say so.** Three of the four handlers touch six or seven
offsets. The extents come from construction arguments and the rest is unobserved span - which is
the honest form, not a shortfall.

**The correction is mine and it is against the page.** State 2 read *"`+0` += elapsed"*, and the
arm computes no elapsed time:

```asm
0032E149  call 0035E810          ; RESULT DISCARDED
0032E14E  call 0035E810
0032E153  add  qword ptr [rbx], rax
0032E156  mov  qword ptr [rbx+8], rax
```

`0035E810` is **eight bytes** - `mov rax, [022CA5E0]` / `ret` - an absolute counter getter with no
delta and no side effect. Both calls return the same value, the first is redundant, and **`+0`
accumulates absolute readings**. What that is *for* is not settled, and the page says so instead of
choosing between a running sum and a defect.

Four additions: `+0x28 = min(+0x30, +0x34)`; the `0x800` round-**down** of `+0x2C` in its
signed-bias form; `0046E030`'s fifth argument at `rsp+0x28` at callee entry; `0032E370`'s gated-out
return being the callback pointer rather than zero.

That is an artefact of a callee that takes no arguments - dead registers are dead - and putting it
on the page would invite a reader to think the values mean something. It belongs to the harness's
model, and the page says so rather than omitting it silently.

The pool ends where the list heads begin. Route `ARRAY 0x022C31C0 stride=0x80 count=64`, allocation
`IMAGE`, ctor `0032E450`. **Not written this session**: the field rows want a census, and this
receiver arrives from a *global load inside the body* rather than in a register at entry, which
`receiver_flow_census`'s entry-register model does not express. That is a new seed shape, not a

## Package 147 - the blocker I had just named turned out to be twelve lines (OPUS)

Package 146 closed `REQ-OPUS-EXP109-POLL-PUMP-FINDINGS` with the schema row answered *yes* and
**not written**, because the census could not be run: the pump `0032E070` takes no object
argument. It loads the pending-list head out of `022C51C0` **inside its own body**, so
`receiver_flow_census`'s entry-register model describes the *caller's* `rcx`, which is not the
slot. I called it "a new seed shape, not a quick run" and moved on.

**It was a quick run.** `--seed-global` - a VA whose loaded value is the object, the same abstract
value through a different door - is one branch in the transfer function:

```python
elif (seed_globals and m == "mov" and ... mem.base == X.X86_REG_RIP
      and (ins.address + ins.size + ins.operands[1].mem.disp) in seed_globals):
    ns[d] = ("R", 0)
```

**The regression is the part that matters.** Every earlier census re-runs byte-identical - the
pane child still reaches 486 of 486 with the same thirty offsets - because the branch fires only
when a seed list is supplied. An instrument change that silently moved an old answer would be
worse than the gap it closed.

and is not one. 24 field rows tiling `0x80` exactly; 21 offsets over 71 sites from six seeds, each

**The extent is measured from both ends.** The builder's own loop gives `lea rax,[rax+0x80]` and

### 0xD0 is the minimum widget, and it is the same boundary as the other one (OPUS)

`scan_widget_inplace_extents` finds **five** in-place constructions of extent `0xD0` with a literal
offset. **The negative result first: their handlers are five different functions** - `002B6CE0`,
`002BC310`, `003CA530`, `003FACF0`, `003FC3F0`, each recovered from the `r8` of its own
construction. A shared size and a shared offset do not make a shared type, and here is a five-way
worked example of the rule this store states.

**What they do share is the layout.** All five censuses are exhaustive - 51, 51, 180, 145 and 75
instructions, every one at 100 %. Between them they touch `+0x38`, `+0x50`, `+0x60`, `+0x98`,
`+0x9A`, `+0x9C`, `+0x9E` - **every one a declared Widget header offset** - and then `+0xC0`, which
**all five** touch, and `+0xC2`, which two do. **Nothing else. No offset above `+0xC2` in any of
the five.**

So **`0xD0` is the minimum widget subclass**: Widget's declared rows end at `+0xBC`, `+0xC0` is the
first 16-aligned offset past them, and `0xD0` is that header plus one 16-byte payload of which
these five use two to four bytes.

**And it is the same boundary as this morning's other observation.** `+0xC0` is where a widget's
*own* content begins - whether that content is a scalar (these five) or a nested child (the five
constructions at `+0xC0`, the AB30 panel array, `BattleMenuWidget2DC0`'s `subObject00C0`, and the
address-taken `+0xC0` in four handler censuses today). **Two observations, one rule.**

*Measured and deliberately not overclaimed:* `002B6CE0` and `002BC310` produce **identical
censuses** - same seven offsets, same site counts, 51 instructions each - and are **not** the same
bytes: 14 of 202 differ, the first at `+0x1E`. That is one source template emitted twice with
different rip-relative targets, not one body reached two ways.


## Package 148 - the handler checker went from covering 57 rows to 228 (OPUS)

Package 145's checker re-derived every `exact` row of `widget-message-handlers.tsv` that dispatches
through a **jump table** - 57 of them - and reported the other **201 as UNBACKED**, because
`resolve_switch_arms` reads tables only. That is a fifth of the artifact checked and four fifths
taken on trust.

### The sparse chain is a running subtraction, not a series of compares (OPUS)

```asm
mov ecx, dword ptr [rdx]     ; the message id
sub ecx, 1     / je A        ; id == 1
sub ecx, 1     / je B        ; id == 2      (1 + 1)
sub ecx, 0xa   / je C        ; id == 12     (2 + 10)
sub ecx, 0xc   / je D        ; id == 24     (12 + 12)
cmp ecx, 0x1d  / je E        ; id == 53     (24 + 29)  - a compare does NOT advance the total
mov rcx, rdi / call 005C5230 ; the default: the base widget procedure
```

**The running total after each `sub` IS the id that arm answers**, and a trailing `cmp` tests the
total plus its own immediate *without* advancing it. Treating the two as one shifts every id after
the first compare.

**First pass: 160 of 201 agreed, 24 disagreed - and 20 of the 24 were the row's list minus its
LAST id.** The reason is the tail form: `0027AD70` ends `cmp r8d, 6` / **`jne <default>`**, so id 18
is answered by *falling through*, and a decoder reading only `je` drops the last arm of every such
handler. Modelled, and the count went to **171 agreeing**.

### Where I stopped, and why that is the answer rather than a shortfall (OPUS)

Fifteen still differ, and reading one settled what to do with all of them. `002C2320` opens
`cmp ecx, 8` / `jg <elsewhere>` / `je <arm>` / `cmp ecx, 1` / `jne <default>` - a **three-way
split**. Both 1 and 8 have arms, plus whatever is behind the `jg`. **The row says only `8`; my
decoder said only `1`. Both are incomplete, in different places.**

So those fifteen are reported as **needing a human, explicitly not as STALE**. Wiring a decoder
that reads two of at least four chain shapes in as authoritative would have produced fifteen
verdicts against rows it cannot see all of - which is the mistake this checker already made once
today, when it called three correct rows stale.

**Coverage: 57 table + 171 chain = 228 of 262 `exact` rows now re-derived from the image**, 3
explained by a pre-table literal compare, 15 flagged, 15 unreadable, 1 blocked by a bad extent in
the function list.


## Package 149 - the compiler schedules between the compare and the branch, and ten rows keep only their last id (OPUS)

Two more shapes read, and the second is a finding about the table rather than the decoder.

### A `mov` in the gap was costing five rows (OPUS)

`005565E0` ends its chain `cmp ecx, 7` / **`mov rcx, rsi`** / `je <arm>` - the next call's receiver
hoisted into the delay the compare leaves. My decoder required the branch to be the NEXT
instruction, so it dropped id 25 there and on `0055A340`.

The rule is not a list of mnemonics I happened to think of: **only an instruction that writes
`EFLAGS` ends the search.** A `mov` does not, so the `je` still answers the compare.
**176 agreeing, up from 171**, with `0029BE50` unchanged and both self-test arms passing.

### Ten rows keep only the LAST id of their chain (OPUS)

The remaining disagreements are now all **supersets** - the chain answers every id the row names
and more - and that is one signature, not ten coincidences. **Two verified by hand:**

- `002C2320` opens `cmp ecx, 8` / `jg` / `je` / `cmp ecx, 1` / `jne <default>`. **Ids 1 and 8 both
  have arms; the row says `8`.**
- `005636F0` runs `cmp eax, 0xc` / `jg` / `je`, `cmp eax, 1` / `je`, `cmp eax, 4` / `je`, then
  `add eax, -8` / `cmp eax, 2` / `ja` - **a range test admitting 8, 9 and 10 as well**. The row
  says `12`.

**So the chain list is itself a floor**, and these are reported as *the row under-reports* rather
than rewritten: neither the `jg` subtree nor the range test is followed, and a mechanical rewrite
would replace one incomplete list with another.

### And the last fifteen were the simplest shape of all (OPUS)

The rows with *neither* a table nor a readable chain turned out to compare the id **straight out
of memory**, with no register to track - which is exactly why the register-based walk could not
see them: it waits for a `mov <r>, [rdx]` that never comes.

```asm
00290FF0  cmp dword ptr [rdx], 4     ; the whole handler is eighteen bytes
00290FF3  jne 0x290FFD
00290FF5  mov rax, [rcx + 0x38]
00290FF9  mov byte ptr [rax + 0x5c], 4
00290FFD  jmp 0x3F7F50               ; the base procedure
```

No accumulator; each compare names its id outright. **UNBACKED went from 15 to zero.**

**261 of 262 `exact` rows are now re-derived from the image and every disagreement is
classified**: 57 table, 3 pre-table literal compares, **191 chain**, 10 supersets, **0
unexplained**, **0 unbacked**, 5 `unparsed` stubs counted and not checked. The one row left is
blocked by the bad extent in `functions.tsv` that this checker found and filed.


## Package 150 - three routes that name two types each, and none of them is the same problem (OPUS)

`check_route_uniqueness` is one of the five checkers left unadopted for being red, and its whole
output is six rows across three pairs. Its own remedy sentence is the right one: *a census seeded
from a shared route attributes another type's offsets to the one asked for and reports a LARGER
result rather than an error, so each needs its restriction recorded where a later reader will find
it.* **Every one of the three is a route that is TRUE and INCOMPLETE, and the missing half is
different each time.**

**`CHAIN ActorStorageRecord +0xA8 stride=0x28` — `VmResultEntry` and `ActorWaitSlot` are the same
array, and one is a strict subset of the other.** Same record, same offset, same stride, same
count. `VmResultEntry` declares two named fields; `ActorWaitSlot` declares **both of them at the
same offsets with the same meanings**, plus nine more. Seeding the subset reports the same bytes
with nine fields missing — which reads as a smaller type rather than an error.

### The finding, which is the mechanism and not the ten corrections - 2026-09-20 (OPUS)

Every one of the ten rows kept **exactly the pivot id of the binary-search root** - the
`cmp <id>, K` immediately after `mov ecx, dword ptr [rdx]`, whose `jg` opens the high half and
whose `je` takes K's own arm - and nothing past it. Four kept 12; the six read today keep 18, 8,
16, 12, 10 and 8. Whatever produced the `exact` column read the first compare after the id load
and stopped. That is one mechanism, not ten coincidences, and it bounds how far the other `exact`
rows can be trusted without re-derivation: only where the dispatch *is* that first compare.

| handler | row said | answers | what the row was missing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0027F5D0` | 18 | 1,2,15,18,19,288 | `jg` subtree + running subtraction |
| `002C2320` | 8 | 1,8,9,10,12,14,18,19,287 | `jg` subtree + 11-wide range test into a table |
| `002D70F0` | 16 | 1,2,15,16,18,19,288 | two running subtractions; tail-jump default |
| `003FF360` | 12 | 1,8,10,12,18,19,285 | `sub ecx,7` low half + `jg` subtree |
| `00557DB0` | 10 | 1,2,10,12,15,18,19,20,285 | **three** levels of binary search |
| `00565E00` | 8 | 1,8,9,10,12,13,14,16,18,287 | `jg` subtree + 10-wide range test into a table |

**A range test's width is not its id set.** `002C2320`'s window admits eleven ids and five of its
table entries point at the default arm, so it answers six; `00565E00`'s admits ten and three point
at the default, so it answers seven. Both tables sit *past* the listed body end - `002C2C18` is
the first byte after one, `0056657C` is two bytes after the other - which is where MSVC puts them
and is data, not code harvested through a boundary.

**The termination problem is real and `00557DB0` contains it outright.** Its id-1 arm loads
`movzx ecx, byte ptr [rbp+0x37d]` and runs its own `sub ecx,1` / `je` chain over 0, 1, 2 and 4 -
the exact shape of the message dispatch, over a different value, in the same register. A tree
walker following `je` targets would have harvested four message ids out of a byte of widget state.
That is why this was six hand reads rather than a better decoder, and it is the same failure that
made the general comparison-tree walker worse than the flat one earlier today.

**The decoder and the hand read agree where they overlap.** For all six, the flat chain
`check_widget_message_ids` reports is exactly the low half I read - `1,2,15,18` / `1,8` /
`1,2,15,16` / `1,8,10,12` / `1,2,10` / `1,8`. Every id added comes from a shape it refuses to
follow. The corrections are additions, not repairs.

to look alike; they are eight slots selected by one dispatcher.** `00564B90` is 186 bytes and does
all of it:

   slot 0, so an unknown id silently aliases the first slot.

   (`00564BD9`) and the write base (`00564C39`)**; the two RIP displacements differ and resolve to
   one address, which is worth stating because it looks like two tables at a glance.

   `jne 00564C2C` skips the `lea r9` arms entirely, so `r9` stays the `xor r9d, r9d` from entry and
   the rebuild passes a **null handler**, which the constructor folds to `005C5230`
   (`0024662B`–`00246641`). A rebuilt slot is therefore a widget whose procedure is the no-op.
4. Otherwise an 11-wide jump table at `00564C4C` over `id - 0x405` picks the handler, and three of
   its eleven arms (`0x40A`, `0x40B`, `0x40C`) go to the common tail with no handler at all.

`00563B10`, `0x40F` → `00563D20`.

### `_5380`'s three pools declared - 2026-09-20 (OPUS)

**The mechanism is the same three times**, and it is what makes the three pointer fields make
sense: each channel is a **fixed slot pool plus an active singly-linked list**. The pool is an array
in the parent, each element carries an in-use flag a linear scan tests for a free slot, and a
claimed element is appended to a list threaded through element `+0x18` whose head is the channel's
pointer.

| pool | base | slots | flag at element | list head | scan |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | `+0x000` | 12 × `0x30` | `+0x0F` byte | `ptr0420` | `00289C00` |
| B | `+0x240` | 6 × `0x28` | `+0x16` word | `ptr0428` | `00289E80` |
| C | `+0x330` | 6 × `0x28` | `+0x12` word | `ptr0430` | `00289FB6` |

All three append identically — `mov rcx,[rsi+head]` / `test` / store if null, else walk `[rcx+0x18]`
to the tail (`00289CA8`, `00289EEE`, `0028A021`). **That is what `ptr0420`/`ptr0428`/`ptr0430` are:
list heads**, not the slot interiors the overrun reading had made of them.

**Declared:** `ManagerSub5380PoolAEntry` (`0x30`), `PoolBEntry` (`0x28`), `PoolCEntry` (`0x28`), and
three array fields replacing five parent rows — including `flag0256` and `subAddr0342`, which were
element-0 flags rather than fields of this type.

**A and B and C are three types, not one reused.** B and C are both `0x28` and put their flag at
**different** element offsets, `+0x16` against `+0x12`, and C writes a dword at `+0x14` that B never
touches.

`[rbx+0x20]` *after* `003EFD00` renders into `+0x10`, which would truncate anything longer — so
`+0x18` is the next pointer being nulled and the text field is the **eight** bytes `+0x10..+0x18`,
not `0x18` of buffer.

`04-Actor-Entity/Battle-Unit/the-battle-unit-field-map.md` already records `00289BD0` as the

refuse to project because their parent `ManagerSub0209BE80_5380` has no census of its own — its

precisely the shape where a `u16` at `+0x106` is the safer reading — a compiler reading a packed
field's high byte looks identical.

**It is not a single read.** `00263B80` is an **eight-byte function** whose entire body is that
load:

```
00263B80  movzx eax, byte ptr [rcx + 0x107]
00263B87  ret
```

A dedicated accessor returning the byte zero-extended, and it is live — a rel32 scan of `.text`
finds **three** direct call sites. Two settle what the value is:

| site | what it does with the result |
| --- | --- |
| `002C8876` | `call` / `cmp al, 1` / `je` — compared against 1, a standalone small value |
| `0034FCCC` | `call` / `movzx edx, al` — forwarded as a **byte argument**, tail `jmp 0026B4E0` |

**Nothing recombines it with `+0x106`.** A `u16` at `+0x106` would not be served by an 8-byte
accessor returning only its high byte zero-extended; callers would read the word. **So the word-wide
initialiser proves nothing about extent** — and it was the only thing that ever suggested a `u16`.
`initByte107` confidence `UNKNOWN` → `PROVEN`; `+0x106` unchanged and still written-never-read.

**One caution recorded with it:** a linear decode started twelve bytes before `002A7204` lands
mid-instruction and produces nonsense, so nothing is claimed about what that third site does. The
rel32 scan finds the call; the surrounding read does not.

### `census_field_accessors.py` — the image's dedicated field accessors - 2026-09-20 (OPUS)

The `ActorStorageRecord` result generalises, so I built the instrument instead of repeating the hand
search 59 times. **An accessor is better evidence of a field than an access is:** an access says
some instruction touched those bytes; a whole function that exists to return exactly those bytes at
exactly that width says the compiler was given a member and emitted a getter for it.

Over **9,921 listed bodies of ≤ 24 bytes**, it finds **237 accessors — 149 GETTER, 88 SETTER**.
By width `1B:56 2B:9 4B:117 8B:55`; by receiver `rcx:235, rdx:2`. Two bodies were skipped because
their listed length ends mid-instruction — counted, not guessed at.

The rules are deliberately tight: one load or store through an argument register at a displacement,
then `ret`. **A function that loads and then tests is not an accessor** — it is a predicate, and its
width tells you about the test rather than the member.

**The control is built in and mandatory.** `00263B80` — read by hand and published in `ad3a64f8a` —
must come back as an 8-byte GETTER of 1 byte at `+0x107`, and the run exits 2 if it does not. It
passes. An absence from a scan that cannot find a known positive is worthless.

address stored in data.

address is *shaped* like a table slot — that is not proof of a vtable, only that a dispatcher could
read it. And a zero caller count excludes calls through a register loaded by any route these sweeps
do not follow, so **UNREFERENCED means unreferenced by these two sweeps, never "dead."**

### The escape check: built, failed its control, NOT registered - 2026-09-20 (OPUS)

Resume 173 named the escape check as the missing half — the route both S-01 and S-14 close by hand
and nothing in my kit does. Built it as `check_interior_escape.py`. **It fails its control and is
deliberately not registered as a gate.**

S-14's page gives an exact control: *"the only displacement that ever escapes is `+0x000`"*, at
`00302D2A`, `00324957`, `00324DB5`, `00336869`. Run over the 199-function battle-unit closure, my
version reproduces **0 of 4**, and three separate reasons were traced rather than guessed:

1. **A pointer returned by a call is never tainted.** `00302D2A` stores `rax` straight from
   `call 002367A0`, an accessor returning the object. The page seeded by *"tainting the accessor's
   return value"*; this does not.
2. **The object may live in a non-argument register.** At `00324957` the store is
   `mov [r13], r14`, and the body opens `mov rcx, r14` — `r14` held it first, and only the
   closure's declared `argreg` is tracked.
3. `00336869` sits in `00336710`, which this closure does not contain — a population difference,
   not a tracking gap.

**And its only "finding" was a false positive.** `00311FBB` `mov [rsp+0x50], rdi` is a **stack
spill**, followed immediately by `lea rcx, [rsp+0x40]` building a local record to pass on — a
handoff the closure already follows, not a pointer left where a later reader finds it. `rsp`/`rbp`
destinations are now excluded, so the report is honestly **empty** rather than wrong.

**Why it is not registered.** It misses three of four known positives and found one spurious. A
checker in `run_gates` whose silence cannot be trusted is worse than no checker, because people run
it and believe it. It ships with a loud failing control and `exit 2`, usable to **confirm** escapes
it does find and never to promote a span on its silence.

**This does not weaken the two re-tests published above** — neither claimed the escape route was
closed; both recorded explicitly that it was not repeated. The instrument's absence was already in
their limits.

### The escape check, second attempt: still 0 of 4, and why - 2026-09-20 (OPUS)

Fixed the defect the failures pointed at. The object is now tracked as a **set of registers** —
`holds` maps every register currently carrying `object + d`, propagating across copies and `lea`,
each dying on its own write. The old version tracked only the closure's declared `argreg` and killed
everything when that register was written, which is what a compiler does on entry: `003247F0` parks
the argument in a callee-saved register and restores it later with `mov rcx, r14`.

**It is still 0 of 4, and instrumenting the body says why — a limit I had already written down.**

```
00324857  lea  r14, [rdi + 0xbc0]        ; rdi is the unit -> r14 = unit + 0xBC0
00324868  mov  [rsp + 0x30], r14         ; SPILLED to the frame
...
00324957  mov  [r13], r14                ; r14 reloaded from somewhere; not tracked
```

At `00324957` the tracker holds `{rdi: 0, rdx: 0}` — **`r14` is gone**, dropped when it was written
between the spill and the store. The section below traces what overwrote it and settles the cause:
not stack taint, but **a pointer returned by a call**, which this tool never taints. Handoffs rose
4 → 448 with the register-set fix, so the change was real; it just does not reach this shape.

### A contradiction raised against S-14, then closed AGAINST ME - 2026-09-20 (OPUS)

Seeing `lea r14, [rdi + 0xbc0]` spilled at `00324868` and `mov [r13], r14` at `00324957`, I was about
to file a contradiction: the page says the only escaping displacement is `+0x000`, and this looked
like `unit + 0xBC0` escaping. **Reading the rest of the body says the page is right and I was wrong.**

```
00324857  lea  r14, [rdi + 0xbc0]     ; r14 = unit + 0xBC0
00324868  mov  [rsp + 0x30], r14      ; spilled - and NEVER RELOADED into r14
00324920  mov  ecx, r12d              ; an index
00324923  call 00236820               ; index -> unit accessor
00324928  mov  r14, rax               ; ** r14 OVERWRITTEN by the return value **
0032493E  mov  rcx, rax               ; the return passed AS A RECEIVER to 002FFEF0,
00324941  call 002FFEF0               ;   which is what proves rax is a whole unit
00324957  mov  [r13], r14             ; stores THAT - displacement +0x000
```

The spill is a red herring: `[rsp+0x30]` is never read back into `r14`. The stored value is a unit
pointer returned by an accessor, so the escape is at **`+0x000`, exactly as the page states**, and
`00302D2A` has the same shape — a store of `rax` straight out of the sibling accessor `002367A0`.

**So the miss is limitation #1, which this file already printed**: *"a pointer returned by a call is
never tainted"*. The page seeded taint from the accessor's RETURN VALUE; the tool does not, so it
cannot see any of these sites. No contradiction exists, nothing published moves, and
`OPUS-CONTRA-S14-ESCAPE-DISPLACEMENT` is **withdrawn before it was filed anywhere but here** — kept
in the record because a retracted suspicion is cheaper to read than to re-derive.

**One real defect in my own tool did fall out of it.** The store at `00324957` goes to `r13`, and
`00324914 lea r13, [rsp + 0x70]` makes `r13` a pointer into the CURRENT FRAME — a local array the
loop walks with `add r13, 8`. My escape test excludes `rsp`/`rbp` destinations as spills, but it
compares the *base register only*, so a frame address laundered through another register defeats the
exclusion. The tool would call this an escape and the page-style hand run calls it one too; the two
agree here only by accident. Frame-address laundering is now a named hole, not a silence.

### The escape check now PASSES its control at 3 of 4, which is the ceiling - 2026-09-20 (OPUS)

Both named causes were fixed and the control went **0 → 2 → 3 of 4**, where 3 is the maximum
reachable. The escapes found are **3 stores at exactly one displacement, `+0x000`**, at
`00302D2A 00324957 00324DB5` — S-14's conclusion re-derived rather than restated.

1. **Taint `rax` after a call to an accessor that returns the object** (`--returns`, supplied per
   type). This is how most bodies obtain the object at all. 0 → 2 of 4.
2. **Stop exiting the scan when the tainted set empties.** With return taint an accessor called later
   re-seeds the object, so quitting at the first moment nothing is tainted discards every escape
   after the object's register is first reused. That is exactly what hid `00302D2A` — a store of the
   accessor's return **into a global**, `0x125A` bytes into `00301AD0`. 2 → 3 of 4.

`00336869` is in `00336710`, which the closure does not contain: **excluded by population, not
forgiven**. A membership test settles which bucket each site is in, and it corrected me twice —
`extents()` holds a **length, not an end address**, and my first test therefore reported all four
sites out of population, including two the tool was demonstrably finding.

**What this does NOT license.** The result depends entirely on `--returns`, which is supplied by
hand; given none, the tool taints nothing through a call, finds nothing, and its silence means only
that it was not told where to look. The control now refuses rather than passing in that case. Volatile
registers are dropped at every call, correct for the ABI but lossy when a callee preserves one. And
frame-address laundering (`lea r13,[rsp+0x70]` then `mov [r13], rX`) still defeats the spill
exclusion — `00324957` is that shape, and S-14's hand run counts it as an escape too, so the two
agree there by accident.

**The two re-tests published in this package are unaffected.** Neither claimed the escape route was
closed; both recorded explicitly that it was not repeated. Closing it for `BattleUnit` and

**Separating the two classes is what made the count mean anything.** Before it, the check reported
6 "escapes" over the battle-unit closure; all but one were stores into **one local array at
`[rsp+0x70]`**, filled from five branches of `003247F0`. A local collection buffer is not a pointer
left where a later reader can find it. Frame-derived registers are now tracked through `lea` and
copies, so `lea r12,[rsp+0x70]` / `lea r12,[r12+rax*8]` / `mov [r12], rbx` classifies correctly —

in that body. The `+0xBC0` store I once suspected of contradicting S-14 lands here too: a spill,
correctly classified, and the page remains right.

`+0x6D4 +0x6D8 +0xBC0`. Those are spills of an interior pointer into the body's own frame, which is
exactly what the page's rule is not about — the rule applies to escapes only, and counting spills
broke the rule's own test.

**Two new seeding routes, because an argument register is not how most bodies get an object.**

1. `derive_object_accessors.py` — a function returns the object if its return value is passed onward
   into a closure member's **proved** argreg, confirmed from **≥2 distinct bodies**. Over the

into, is still a span nothing **explains** — no meaning, no representation, no invariant. All nine

### A false positive in my own derivation, found by using its output - 2026-09-20 (OPUS)

`derive_object_accessors.py` **admitted `0020E600` as a battle-unit accessor. It is not an accessor
for anything.** Its whole body is ten bytes:

```
0020E600  mov eax, ecx            ; a 32-bit BYTE OFFSET, not a scaled index
0020E602  add rax, [rip -> 01F83530]
0020E609  ret
```

That is the engine's **universal base-relative reference decoder**, and **the store already
documents it** — `ActorWaitSlot.targetRef` records *"a BASE-RELATIVE reference … `0020E600` resolves
it as `arg + *(01F83530)`"*. It returns a pointer into a shared arena; what type lives there depends
entirely on the offset handed to it, which is why the loot tier code calls the same function at
`00319A86`. **The ≥2-distinct-bodies rule cannot catch this**: that guard is aimed at accidents, and
a universal decoder legitimately feeds many consumers in many bodies.

`is_universal_decoder` now refuses the **shape** — a body ≤24 B, no call or branch, containing an
`add r64, [rip+X]` — so a sibling decoder is caught too. Re-run: `0020E600` **REFUSED**, the
hand-verified `00236820` still **ADMITTED**, the other three unchanged.

**I checked rather than assumed whether this touched what I published.** Re-running the escape check
with the decoder excluded gives an **identical result**: 1 true escape at `00302D2A`, 17 frame-local
at `+0x0 +0x6D4 +0x6D8 +0xBC0`. Only the handoff count moves, 376 → 369, which is exactly what
dropping the decoder's consumers should do. **`20f8c645e` stands as published.**

**L1 and L2 are NOT satisfied.** `final_audits` 0/30; `engine_explained` 39.31 %; `Runtime` 2/412.

### S-16 `SpawnKeepImage +0x0004`: NOT padding, and that is the point - 2026-09-20 (OPUS)

Opened S-16 next: its types are in better shape than S-33's were — `SpawnRecord` (`0x250`) and
`SpawnGroupLedger` (`0x18`) are both **TYPE RESOLVED L2** — so the gap there is the contract, not the
layout. The exception is **`SpawnKeepImage`, `0x20010` at only SIGNATURE RESOLVED L1**, which tiles
exactly but leaves **12 unexplained bytes at `+0x0004`**, between the two field ids and the first
bank at `+0x10`.

**The tempting answer is wrong, and saying so is the contribution.** Having just closed two spans on
S-33 as alignment padding, the obvious move is to reuse that reasoning. **It does not apply.** The
banks are `uint8[65536]` — alignment **1** — and the ids are `uint16` — alignment **2**. The
strictest member alignment in this type is therefore **2**, and *nothing in the declared layout
forces a 16-byte header*. Unlike `WorldLootPickupNode`, where an 8-byte pointer at `+0x10` forced the
hole, **here the compiler would emit no padding at all**. The 16-byte header is a deliberate layout
choice, and those 12 bytes are either reserved or fields nobody has found.

**What the initialiser shows.** `00233440` (260 B) opens with
`xor edx,edx / mov r8d,0x20010 / call 00861EC0` — a **memset of the whole image to zero** — then
fills bank 2 at `+0x10` and bank 1 at `+0x10010` with `movups` copy loops from two rip-relative
sources. So the 12 bytes are **zeroed by a bulk write and never individually written here**. A bulk
write that happens to cover a span does not explain it; that is exactly what
`check_bulk_write_lifetime.py` exists to distinguish.

**The page states the size without explaining it.** Line 420: *"a 16-byte header holding the two
field-id registers"*; line 843 gives the `lea +0x10` / `lea +0x10010` / `memset 0x20010` evidence.
The header's size is established; its contents past `+0x04` are not.

**NEXT STEP, not taken here**: the S-33 method needs adapting, because this type is **EMBED in
`SavePayload` at `+0xE240` and `+0x2E450`** and is reached through a register, not a fixed
rip-relative array — so the array-route scan that settled the loot spans cannot seed it. It needs a
closure over the keep-image holders, then a displacement census of `+0x04`…`+0x0F`.

**The row stays `DISCOVERED`.** Twelve bytes bulk-zeroed and otherwise untouched by one function is
not an explanation.

### S-16 `SpawnKeepImage +0x0004` - WITHDRAWN, I MEASURED THE WRONG OBJECT - 2026-09-20 (OPUS)

The twelve-byte header span is now characterised. **It is not padding**, and the `WorldLootPickupNode`
answer closed earlier today must not be reused: the banks are `uint8[65536]` (align 1) and the ids
`uint16` (align 2), so the strictest member alignment is **2** and nothing forces a 16-byte header —
a compiler would emit none.

**Measured.** A byte-prefiltered scan of all **38,161 bodies** for 32 payload-relative patterns —
both images' base plus every header offset `+0x1`…`+0xF` — returns **8 sites, every one
`lea rcx, [payload + 0xE240 / 0x2E450]`**, and **zero** at any header interior offset.

**All three direct consumers are bulk.** `00233440` memsets the whole `0x20010` then fills the two
banks. `0025D8E0` and `00269A20` are a **symmetric staging pair** moving `4 × 0x80 = 0x200` bytes —
the whole header included — out of and into **the same global buffer `02099FF0`**, both rip targets
computed rather than eyeballed. An image-wide scan of that buffer: **7 references in 6 functions, all
to the base, 1 of 17 addresses referenced** — zero reach its sixteen interior bytes. Three further
sites memset it.

**One route remains open, and it is named.** `0026CB31` does `lea rax,[02099FF0]` then
`mov [rdi+0x60], rax` — it **stores the buffer pointer into a descriptor**, and a consumer reached
through that descriptor could read the header. A displacement scan cannot follow a pointer, so
"never interpreted" is a **floor**. Closing it is the interior-escape problem this session already
built tooling for, pointed at a different object.

**The row stays `DISCOVERED`.** Better characterised is not explained, and the layout says these
bytes are not padding, so an explanation is still owed.

### The retraction, and the contradiction under it - 2026-09-20 (OPUS)

**The section above is withdrawn. Its measurement was of a different object.** Nothing from it
reached `fields.tsv`: the note was written, then stripped before publication, and the file is clean
against HEAD. The queue is what caught it.

**What went wrong.** The `SpawnKeepImage` row states its two instances sit at **payload** `+0xE240`
and `+0x2E450`. I scanned for those displacements, found 8 sites, and read them as keep-image
accesses. They are not. Every site takes its base from `002EF620`, and:

```
002EF620   lea rax,[rip+0x1ECB319]; ret   ->  021BA940
002EF640   lea rax,[rip+0x1E74C39]; ret   ->  02164280      the active save buffer
002EF2B0   = 002EF640() + 0x200           ->  02164480      so PAYLOAD = BUFFER + 0x200
```

So a **buffer**-relative `+0xE240` is a **payload**-relative `+0xE040` — which is exactly where
`script-variables-and-their-storage-classes.md` says `scratch2`, the 0x200-byte group persistent
bank at `02099FF0`, is exported and imported **by the very two functions I traced**, `0025D8E0` and
`00269A20`. **I measured scratch2's round trip and attributed it to the keep image.**

**The contradiction is real and is filed** as `OPUS-CONTRA-KEEPIMAGE-VS-SCRATCH2-COORDINATES`: the
two documents disagree by exactly the payload offset, and **both cannot be payload-relative** —
`scratch2` is `0x200` bytes and `SpawnKeepImage` is `0x20010`, so they cannot share an address. I did
**not** re-derive the containment check, so I am not asserting which row is wrong, only that the
frame must be stated wherever these offsets are quoted. A third frame is in play too: `002EF620`
returns a *different* buffer, `0x566C0` past the active one.

**What survives from that section**, because it never depended on the frame:

* **The span is not alignment padding.** Banks `uint8[65536]` (align 1), ids `uint16` (align 2), so
  the strictest member alignment is 2 and nothing forces a 16-byte header. Layout-only, still true.
* **`00233440` is genuinely the keep-image initialiser** — it takes the image in `rcx` and memsets
  `0x20010`, which matches the type's size and cannot be scratch2's `0x200`. It bulk-zeroes the
  header and never field-writes it.

**What does NOT survive**: the staging-buffer story, the `02099FF0` round trip, the
`0026CB31` descriptor route, and the "persisted but never interpreted" verdict. All of that is
`scratch2`'s and belongs to S-07's material, not S-16's.

**The span is back to unmeasured**, and cannot be measured until the frame is settled — the scan
coordinates depend on it. The row is untouched and stays `DISCOVERED`.

**The lesson is the one my own rules already state**: a row's wording is a claim about a coordinate
frame, and an offset without its frame is not an address. I had the falsifier available the whole
time — `002EF2B0` is literally `GetActiveBuffer() + 0x200` — and did not read it until the numbers
disagreed.

**L1 and L2 are NOT satisfied.** `final_audits` 0/30; `engine_explained` 39.31 %; `Runtime` 2/412.

`SEMANTICALLY IDENTIFIED` — the content *is* established, it is simply conditional.

**2. My write census is a FLOOR, and §4 proves it.** It tracks the record pointer from `rcx` across
register copies only, so a store through a base it does not follow is invisible. §4 records that
classes 14 and 15 write **`+0x42`** as a `u16` — and **my census has no store there**. So "23
displacements" is a lower bound, now stated as one on the type row.

**The tail claim survives that limit**, because it does not rest on my census alone: FABLE's read
census independently reports that **no caller reads anything from `+0x61` on** except `00273BA0`,
the wholesale copier. Two instruments, different directions, same boundary.

**The lesson repeats today's other one.** I derived widths from the binary and treated the result as
complete when it was a floor; the page's §4 was the falsifier and I read it after declaring rather
than before. Mapping existing knowledge first is in the goal for exactly this reason.

### `ItemClassDescriptor`: the offset slots are 8 bytes carrying a 32-bit value - 2026-09-20 (OPUS)

§4's formula block calls the descriptor `InventoryClassDescriptor` and types `+0x00`/`+0x18`/`+0x28`
as `u32`; the store registers the same `0x58` structure as **`ItemClassDescriptor`** with those three
as `uint64`. **Both are partly right, and neither states the representation.** The rebase pass
`0030B6A0` shows it in adjacent instructions:

```
0030B6A5  xor  r11d, r11d            ; r11 = 0
0030B6C0  cmp  qword [r8], r11       ; tests ALL EIGHT BYTES for empty
0030B6C5  mov  eax, dword [r8]       ; loads only the LOW 32 BITS as the offset
0030B6C8  add  eax, r10d             ; a THIRTY-TWO BIT add with the runtime base
0030B6CB  mov  qword [r8 + 8], rax   ; stored as a full 64-bit pointer
```

So the **slot is 8 bytes** and the **value is a 32-bit offset in its low half** — the zero test is
only correct while the high half stays zero. And because `add eax, r10d` zero-extends,
**every resolved region pointer is forced below 4 GB by construction**. A reconstruction resolving
these with 64-bit arithmetic would diverge the moment a region landed above 4 GB. Recorded on all
six rows — the three offset slots and the three pointer slots they feed.

The same loop also settles `+0x40`: `mov [r8+0x40], r9d` then `add r9d, [r8+0x3C]` makes it the
**exclusive prefix sum of `itemCount`** across the fifteen rows, which is what the store's
`firstIndex` and the page's `cumulativeBase` each name from one side.

**Not filed as a contradiction**, because it is not one: the two documents describe the same bytes at
different granularities and the binary reconciles them. What was missing was the representation, and
that is now in the store.

**A naming gap remains, and it is real**: `InventoryClassDescriptor` appears in a formula block with
**no row in `NAME-EQUIVALENCES.tsv`** pointing at `ItemClassDescriptor`, so a reader searching either
name will not find the other. I do not hold that file; noted here rather than edited.

**L1 and L2 are NOT satisfied.** `final_audits` 0/30; `engine_explained` 39.31 %; `Runtime` 2/412.

### An actor's collision radius is an ORIENTED ELLIPSE, not a circle - 2026-09-20 (OPUS)

Chasing an adoption request into `003DA730` produced a result worth more than the adoption. The
store already had `MovementContext +0x050` / `+0x054` / `+0x058` as two radius lanes and an angle.
**Reading the 244-byte body confirms that order and says what the numbers mean:**

```
003DA73E  movss xmm6, [rcx + 8]      ; orientation, at cap+0x08
003DA743  mulss xmm6, [01CEBC9C]     ; = -1.0 -> rotate by MINUS the angle, into the ellipse frame
003DA775  call 00861F08              ; cos
003DA780  call 00861F0E              ; sin
003DA7C1  movss xmm0, [rbx]          ; semi-axis a, at cap+0x00
003DA7CD  movss xmm2, [rbx + 4]      ; semi-axis b, at cap+0x04
003DA7C5  movss xmm1, [01CEBBA8]     ; = 1.0, divided by each SQUARED semi-axis
```

Both constants resolved by computation. With `(u, v)` the rotated `(dx, dz)` — taken from the
points' `+0x00` and `+0x08` lanes, so **y is ignored and this is an XZ metric** — the tail returns

```
(u² + v²) / ( v²/a² + u²/b² )
```

which is exactly the **squared distance from the ellipse centre to its boundary along `p2 − p1`**.
`003DA7BF` returns 0 when `u² + v² ≤ 0`. `003A1D30` takes `sqrt(|·|)`, and the caller adds
`cap+0x0C` — so **an actor's effective radius is direction-dependent**: an oriented ellipse's
boundary distance plus a constant margin.

**Why it matters for reconstruction.** A reimplementation treating the radius as a scalar circle
agrees with the original **only when the two semi-axes are equal**. Two actors approaching on
different bearings get different separations from the same numbers — a divergence that would look
like a physics bug and be almost impossible to trace back to a field-meaning error.

**The rows are corroborated, not renamed** — and that is the point. The executed record I was asked
to adopt states the lane order the other way round; taking it verbatim would have renamed all three.
Filed as `OPUS-CONTRA-EXP138-DA730-LANES-ARE-SHIFTED`.

**Honest limit**: this is a **static** read. Because the one executed record covering these bodies
disagrees on lane order, the corroboration is static-plus-store, **not** static-plus-executed, and
the row says so.

**L1 and L2 are NOT satisfied.** `final_audits` 0/30; `engine_explained` 39.31 %; `Runtime` 2/412.
